articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' QB/TE/DEF/K Blueprint for Week 10
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the onesies — QB, TE, DEF and K — for Week 10.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be a WR column , an RB column and this combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

Not all players are listed in the markets.

1. Josh Allen (at NYJ) - 23.7 proj. points

2. Brock Purdy (at DAL) - 22 proj. points

Purdy remains near the top of the league as fantasy's QB4 (22.4 PPG) on the back of elite efficiency, posting +0.31 EPA per dropback (QB2). His secret fantasy sauce is adding 25 rushing yards and the occasional ground score when the offense feels stuck. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are horrific defensively, allowing opposing QBs to average 19.9 fantasy points per contest. San Francisco enters this road tilt as 3.5-point road favorites with a massive implied team total of 29.5 points (second). Purdy is an elite QB1.

3. Joe Burrow (vs. PIT) - 20.7 proj. points

Burrow enters Week 10 as fantasy's QB1 (26.6 PPG) while delivering +0.27 EPA per dropback (QB4). Over his last four starts, Burrow's output has exploded to 32.1 fantasy points per game and +0.43 EPA per dropback (QB1), tossing 16 passing touchdowns in that heated stretch. Cincinnati leads the NFL with a 66% neutral pass rate (first), and they face a Steelers defense whose opponents pass 60% of the time in neutral situations (first). Pittsburgh has been tough on signal callers overall, allowing the 29th-most half PPR points to QBs (14.3). Even so, Burrow hung 24.6 fantasy points and three touchdowns on them back in Week 3. The Bengals enter as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (fifth).

4. Drake Maye (at DET) - 20.6 proj. points

Maye has surged into the upper tier of fantasy passers, sitting as the QB3 (22.6 PPG) with +0.09 EPA per dropback (QB16). His rushing baseline has been a constant weapon, adding 24.2 rushing yards per game (10th) across nine starts. If we look at Maye's highs and lows, it's clear that there is a sensitivity to opponent strength. He's beaten up on soft opponents since Week 4, and he'll get another one here, potentially with A.J. Brown returning.

The Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (23.6) on the most passing yards (277 YPG). Suddenly-benched QBs Kyler Murray (QB10) and Jacoby Brissett (QB7) had some of their most productive games of the year against them. New England enters this indoor road spot as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 24.5 points (10th).

5. Trevor Lawrence (at TEN) - 19.3 proj. points

Lawrence enters Week 10 as fantasy's QB12 (19.6 PPG) while generating an efficient +0.30 EPA per dropback (QB3). He has thrown multiple passing scores in four of his past five starts.

His Week 10 matchup is as friendly as they come against a Titans defense allowing the fifth-most half PPR points per game to quarterbacks (20.4). They also just traded away their top two players on defense and allow the third-most points to QBs on the ground as a bonus. Jacksonville heads on the road as 10.5-point road favorites carrying a healthy implied team total of 28.5 points (third). This is another eruption spot.

6. Tyler Shough (vs. CAR) - 19.8 proj. points

Shough has at least 15.8 fantasy points in every game except for his date with the Vikings. He was essentially stood up there. Now that he has LT Kelvin Banks back and had the bye week to heal his own fractured left hand, it's time to take Shough seriously as a fantasy QB1. He's the QB8 on the season and could get more production out of his third receiver spot with Jordyn Tyson mixing in. Shough can run when needed, but he may not need to against the Panthers. We'll see if they can return EDGE1, CB1 or CB2 back here. The Saints have a 25.5-point team total (seventh).

7. Dak Prescott (vs. SF) - 17.9 proj. points

Prescott is coming off a 335-yard, two-touchdown performance against Indianapolis and currently checks in as the QB11 in half PPR scoring (19.7 PPG). He has been efficient through the air with +0.18 EPA per dropback (QB9) while generating 264.6 passing yards per game (sixth). He'll welcome back George Pickens in this contest, and the OL is back to full health again. It's one of the most friendly offenses in the NFL, and Prescott is still playing well.

The game environment is great, too. The game total is at a monster 55.5 points, with Dallas as dogs to the 49ers despite having a 26.0-point team total themselves. Kirk Cousins (QB11), Michael Penix (QB8) and Jayden Daniels (QB7) have created a three-game streak of a fantasy QB1 finish.

8. Jared Goff (vs. NE) - 18.2 proj. points

Goff struggled against the Packers and Vikings because of how strong those defenses are, then dudded against the Dolphins in Miami. That was out of character. Goff is now the QB15 in fantasy on QB8 EPA per dropback. The hope is, the worst is behind him.

Up next is a New England defense ranking 14th in half PPR points allowed to opposing QBs (18.7 per game). The Patriots just surrendered a massive 36.2-point explosion to Jordan Love in Week 9 after Caleb Williams posted 22.1 points against them in Week 7. Detroit heads in as 2.5-point German favorites sporting a healthy implied team total of 27 points (fourth).

9. Patrick Mahomes (at ATL) - 19.4 proj. points

The Josh Downs trade will provide him with an answer against man coverage at the underneath and intermediate level. He's just far more polished than anyone else on the Chiefs. Even with poor WR play, Mahomes is the QB14 on QB12 EPA per dropback. He bottomed out against the Seahawks in Week 7 but has otherwise been a low-end QB1 option. The matchup is a clean one, especially with S1 Jesse Bates traded by the Falcons. Joe Burrow gashed them for 278 yards and four scores last week. Kansas City has a 24.5-point team total in this domed vacation.

10. Jayden Daniels (at NYG) - 18.1 proj. points

Daniels is still the QB1 in rushing yards per game (42.0), but they aren't calling designed runs for him since his elbow injury and that average is notably lower than his rookie season (52.4). The Commanders are getting some up-and-down play on go balls from their WRs since Terry McLaurin's injury, but Daniels does enough to hold onto low-end fantasy QB1 value. He's at least cleared 15.0 fantasy points in his five healthy games this year and is the QB13, including that elbow game.

Daniels ran all over the Giants in Week 5 in his return from said injury, posting a season-high 30.3 fantasy points and 103 rushing yards with two scores on the ground. DROY candidate Arvell Reese will look to make sure that doesn't happen here, and I don't like the Commanders' odds of their WRs beating this CB room now. Washington enters this divisional rematch as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 19.5 points (22nd).

11. C.J. Stroud (at CLE) - 16.5 proj. points

I wrote about C.J. Stroud a ton here . He's playing like a top-10 QB and has massively improved against the blitz and pressure.

12. Bryce Young (at NO) - 18.8 proj. points

Young has operated as fantasy's QB9 (20.2 PPG) across eight starts, pairing 272 passing yards per game (fourth) with +0.05 EPA per dropback (QB18). Carolina has stayed committed to the air, operating with the league's third-highest neutral pass rate (60%). He bounced back from a rough two-game stretch (TB and GB) with 24.3 fantasy points and three passing scores against Denver last week. It was an encouraging outing despite not having LG Damien Lewis.

The Saints matchup is one to attack. They've allowed the fifth-most passing yards (256) and sixth-most rushing yards (134). That's tough to do. They can rush the passer but everything else has been a major work in progress, especially just tackling. Young hasn't had a top-16 fantasy game against them throughout his career yet, but the Panthers' No. 12 team total (23.0) suggests that'll change here.

13. Jordan Love (vs. MIN) - 17.4 proj. points

Love has faced the most blitzes in the NFL, and he's handled it very well. He's scored the most touchdowns and compiled the most yards against it, largely throwing downfield darts to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Back in Week 1 against these blitz-crazy Vikings, Love hung 23.5 fantasy points on 387 total yards. He has the aggressiveness and WR talent to make defenses pay when bringing 5+. I can't wait to see if DC Brian Flores continues with a 75% blitz rate or finally cools off.

Love is a riskier start because Minnesota is still only allowing 10.9 fantasy points to QBs this year (easily the least), but Love is the QB2 in passing yards per game (291) and they don't have the run game to really pivot away from what's worked. Green Bay projects for 22.75 points.

articles.title: The Rock's cousin, who is a current top WWE star, admits "nepotism is a great thing"
articles.summary: The Rock has etched his name as one of the biggest WWE superstars of all time.
articles.body: The Rock has etched his name as one of the biggest WWE superstars of all time. While there have been many other names from the Anoa'i family who paved the way, arguably, The Great One is at the top of all of them. This would naturally mean that any of his relatives would get an easy path to enter WWE. In fact, one of his cousins is a top star in WWE today. She is none other than Nia Jax, who made a cold statement about the prevailing debate over nepotism in the company.The Rock's cousin Nia Jax on nepotism favoring her in WWEIn a recent interview on the Battleground Podcast, Nia Jax spoke about her tenure in WWE and how it began. The Irresistible Force said that she initially kept quiet about her rich lineage to find out if she had the merit to become a WWE superstar. Nia said, “Yeah, I mean, I think it’s so, you know, when I first tried out, like, I tried not to let anybody know that I was related to, you know, The Rock and the big Samoan dynasty because I wanted to hopefully get through with my own merits."When asked about fans heckling her for getting opportunities because of The Rock and her family, Jax did not downplay it and said that nepotism was great. She acknowledged that she got an easy entry into the WWE system, but proved her worth in the tryouts and eventually went on to become a top star in the current WWE women's division.She said,"It’s like, well, nepotism is a great thing, you know what I mean? I’m not going to sit there and negate all the accomplishments my family has made in this business. Like, I get to be a part of it. It’s incredible. And I’m not, like, I got an opportunity to try out just like everybody else does, and I made it. So there’s no reason for me not to be proud of my family and not to be proud of what they’ve accomplished."Nia Jax has been a multi-time WWE Women's Champion, one of the few women to compete in a Men's Royal Rumble, and has achieved other major accolades. articles.title: Robbie Avila Expected To Join TCU After Saint Louis Return Denied
articles.summary: TCU is working to add Robbie Avila to its roster after the former Saint Louis player was cleared to play but barred from returning to the Billikens.
articles.body: TCU is working to add center Robbie Avila to its roster after the former Saint Louis player was cleared to play by a judge but barred from returning to the Billikens due to roster restrictions. Horned Frogs coach Jamie Dixon said Thursday he was contacted by Avila and his family after the fifth-year senior exhausted "all options to play at Saint Louis" and became aware of the injury situation at TCU. The Horned Frogs are without Texas Tech transfer Luke Bamgboye indefinitely. Dixon said he had informed the team that the school was in the process of finalizing the eligibility of Avila, the reigning Atlantic 10 player of the year who became a sensation for his signature specs at Indiana State. Avila was granted a fifth year under preliminary injunction, but the College Sports Commission ruled he couldn't play for Saint Louis due to the roster restrictions. It was unlikely that Avila would be available for the Horned Frogs against Milwaukee on Friday night. Their next game is at home against Texas A&M on Nov. 19. The Billikens won a school-record 29 games last season behind Avila, reaching the second round of the NCAA Tournament before losing to eventual national champion Michigan. He averaged 12.8 points and 4.5 rebounds last season and has career averages of 14.5 points and 5.5 rebounds over four seasons — two each with Indiana State and Saint Louis. The Horned Frogs are 3-0 but needed double overtime for a 100-92 victory over UL Monroe at home on Tuesday. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Italy Stuns France: 3 Takeaways From Thursday's Nations League Matches
articles.summary: We had ourselves quite an evening of UEFA Nations League football. From euphoria at the San Siro and consistent Spanish omnipotence in Prague to the coronation of an English star at Wembley.
articles.body: We had ourselves quite an evening of UEFA Nations League football. From euphoria at the San Siro and consistent Spanish omnipotence in Prague to the coronation of an English star at Wembley. Here are my takeaways from Thursday’s action in the Nations League: 1. Italy Finally Broke Through It was an incredibly important victory for Italy. Not perfect. Not beautiful. In fact, there were many mistakes, including another awful error from keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and a missed penalty from one of the Esposito brothers in forward Sebastian. But none of that will matter because, in the end, under the skies of Milan and the iconic San Siro, Italy came out victorious thanks to a trait they know too well: passion and a will to get the job done. There will of course be bigger evenings and nothing will heal the wounds of missing a third straight World Cup, but on a night where Roberto Mancini’s Azzurri wanted to make a statement against the mighty France, it ended with a smile on the faces of all Italians with a 3-1 victory thanks to grit and hunger. It was a night of desire as opposed to substance as Italy relinquished possession but not control. Mancini’s decision to bring on Inter stalwart winger Federico Dimarco for Monza’s Nicolò Cambiaghi in the 62nd minute proved to be a masterstroke as it was his assist that provided the goal for midfielder Davide Frattesi. Another penalty was added and this time, striker Pio Esposito made it 3-1. Italy now sits atop of its group with a hope of getting something over Belgium in order to secure a place in the quarterfinals. France just needs a point, so despite the loss, manager Zinedine Zidane knows it sits in a good place as it gets ready for Türkiye. But tonight was about Italian poetry and, once again, Azurri rejoiced. It’s been a long time since we have seen that happen. 2. It's All About Kane It wasn’t a 7-0 thrashing, but England came out with a 2-1 win over a valiant Croatia at Wembley, but the real story was an evening for superstar striker Harry Kane, who celebrated his record-breaking 126th appearance for the national team with a goal, scoring from the spot. Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers opened the scoring in the 24th-minute, but centerback Jarell Quansah allowed Croatia's Petar Sučić to equalize later in the second half. But five minutes later, Kane, who paraded his Ballon d’Or in front of the Wembley crowd before the match, reclaimed the lead for the third-placed team at the World Cup. This was also an evening of absences for England as Djed Spence, Ezri Konsa and Marc Guéhi all missed out, so defensively, Thomas Tuchel had to shuffle a few things. The German manager probably wanted a clean sheet, but when you have a rotated lineup of Lewis Hall, Dan Burn, the aforementioned Quansah and Trent Alexander-Arnold, I think he’ll be reasonably happy on defense. Hall, in particular, was very strong. But again, this was about Kane and an evening he will never forget. Next up? A mighty battle in Madrid against Spain. 3. No Slowing Down Spain The World Cup champions took care of business against Czechia thanks to a penalty from midfielder Alex Baena (one of my favorite players right now in Europe) and a stoppage-time second goal from Marc Pubill off the bench, both who play for Atlético de Madrid. That’s now 43 matches without a loss and 12 straight victories. A record so impressive, I am beginning to feel numb about Spanish results. I almost expect this side to win, no matter the outcome. This wasn’t, however, a perfect painting from Luis de la Fuente’s side as a 1-0 lead stood throughout until the 96th minute. But then again, not all of them are going to be masterpieces and teams like Czechia will aim to make it sticky for a team who likes to play with the ball in an aesthetic rhythm. This was also a match without Lamine Yamal, Mikel Oyarzabal and the perennial leader, Rodri. Pedri, the team’s architect, didn’t even come on until the 76th minute. So we can see from tonight that it was a rotated side looking to keep the train moving against a weaker opponent. And the table? Spain leads with a perfect 15 points from five matches, five wins, 13 goals scored and five conceded. What awaits now is a delicious battle at the Metropolitano as England visits the Spanish capital on Sunday. The host is the favorite, clearly, but I think if England is able to minimize its mistakes, it can maybe take something from the match. But asking an opponent to be perfect against Spain is the equivalent of swimming in an ocean during a storm. At some point, no matter how hard you fight, you will find yourself fighting against an overwhelming force that won’t let you breathe. But if there’s a team that could maybe disrupt the artistry, as we saw in the last window, it’s England. It should be a fantastic match.

articles.title: Tom Brady Shares Ideal International Soccer Stadium To Host An NFL Game
articles.summary: Tom Brady would have loved to play an international NFL game in this Italian soccer stadium.
articles.body: Tom Brady played in four international games over his decorated 23-year career. He played two in London before playing a game in Mexico City in 2017. He was also part of the NFL's first game in Germany, helping the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get a win in Munich in 2022. But if Brady could have had authority over where to be sent for an international game, he would have selected a site that has yet to host an NFL game. "I would say San Siro in Italy, where AC Milan plays," Brady said when asked where he would most like to play an international game in the most recent edition of #AskTom. Brady attended San Siro to watch AC Milan play Como in February, and left with a lasting impression. "The way those Italian fans cheer all game long," he said. "I would have loved to play in front of them at least once in my career." And Brady offered another Italian stadium that should host an NFL game. "Another bonus one: Lake Como," Brady said. Lake Como, which is also known as Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, is currently home to Como 1907, while the Italian men's national team occasionally plays matches there. The stadium is small, seating 13,600, but it's been called one of the most beautiful stadiums in the world for its lakeside view. As Brady seems to have a particular fondness for Italian stadiums, he couldn't help but envision what San Siro would be like if it hosted a game between heated divisional rivals, like the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers. "That would be pretty frightening," Brady said. "It'd be like Mad Max escaped from LA. I'm not sure many of you guys would make it out of that stadium. It would be a complete zoo." The NFL will head to Munich in Week 10 as Brady's former team, the New England Patriots, will face the Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena, home of FC Bayern Munich. It's the eighth international game of the 2026 season, and the only one in Germany. London has hosted three games. Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro, Paris and Madrid each hosted one earlier this year. Mexico City will host the ninth and final international game of the 2026 season in Week 11. The NFL has yet to travel to Italy for a game, but has expanded to add new cities each season. Milan could certainly be a site for the future. And while Brady wouldn't play in San Siro, he could certainly soak it in as a supporter of the sport. AC Milan currently sits fifth in the Italian Serie A table and has not won the league since 2021-22. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Vivaan Kapoor clinches trap silver, LA quota
articles.summary: Pune: There was a lot of history riding on Vivaan Kapoor when he was shooting for gold in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on
articles.body: Pune: There was a lot of history riding on Vivaan Kapoor when he was shooting for gold in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Thursday.The Jaipur shooter missed creating some, while still becoming part of history, as he clinched silver and an Olympic quota for the Los Angeles Games. Vivaan, 24, became only the fourth Indian to win a World Championships medal in trap and only second after Karni Singh to win a silver.Manavjit Singh Sandhu is the only Indian to have won gold in the event at the Worlds, while Zoravar Singh Sandhu's bronze is the other medal India has won in this category.It was also the first time when two Indians entered a trap final in the World Championships. Other than Vivaan, Udaivir Singh Jaijee also entered the 8-man final, finishing sixth.In the final, Vivaan was in excellent form as he shot 29 clay out of 30. He was tied at 29 with Kuwait's Abdulrahman Al-Faihan as the match progressed to the shoot-off. Vivaan looked good in the shoot-off, but the Kuwaiti shooter too didn't budge and beat the Indian by one shot taking the shoot-off 3-2. The final was a strong field as it had Paris Games gold medallist Nathan Hales and silver medallist Ying Qi of China. While Qi took bronze with 22 hits, Hales got eliminated at the fifth position with the score of 11.Udaivir finished sixth with 11 hits.Earlier, in the qualification round, Vivaan and Udaivir faced a 7-way tie as seven shooters were tied at the score of 120. articles.title: A Season-Saving Win: 3 Takeaways From Commanders Dramatic Victory Over Giants
articles.summary: Here's what we learned from the Commanders' victory over the Giants.
articles.body: METLIFE STADIUM (East Rutherford, N.J.) — The New York Giants haven’t won the NFC East in 15 years, and they had a golden opportunity to take a big step towards ending that drought on Thursday night. But then they blew it. Despite leading the game with less than two minutes to go, they fell apart in crunch time as Jayden Daniels led the Washington Commanders on a late touchdown drive to pull out a dramatic 24-21 victory. They got the game-winning score on a laser pass through traffic from Daniels to Stefon Diggs that became a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds remaining. The Giants had one last chance to pull it out, but J.J. McCarthy’s final pass on a solid night was intercepted. And just like that, the NFC East looks like it might be a race again. The Giants fell to 5-3-1 on the season, closing the gap between them and the second-place Dallas Cowboys (4-5). And the Commanders, at 3-5-1, now hold the tie-breaker advantage over the Giants and are still in the thick of the race. Here are my takeaways from the game that tightened this division up: 1.Jayden Daniels Is As Dangerous As Ever Over the last few weeks, Commanders QB Jayden Daniels has started to round into form, looking a little more like he did two years ago when he was a rookie sensation. That year, he carried a flawed team all the way to the NFC Championship Game. This team, as hard as it is to believe, is even more flawed. But on Thursday night, he showed he’s capable of carrying them too. Daniels was a one-man show at times against the Giants, completing 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards, with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and he ran 10 times for 28 yards, too. He kept the Giants’ punch-less defense on its heels with his ability to scramble. And when they left him unpressured in the pocket — all too often — he picked them apart with his arm. Yeah, he threw two fourth-quarter interceptions, and that wasn’t good. It was also a product of the startling lack of weapons around him. Both passes were force-fed to TE Chig Okonkwo, who has been a disappointment for most of the season. To that point, it was a sign of how few players he had on the field around him who could make and break big plays. But in the end, WR Stefon Diggs — the only receiver who can make big plays on the Commanders' active roster — came through. Diggs took a dart pass over the middle between a couple of Giants defenders, blasted free and ran in for the game-winning score. He finished with six catches for 83 yards. Daniels has no other reliable weapons and no reliable running game and it just doesn’t matter. He’s a weapon all his own. He made it impossible for the Giants pass rush to catch him. He found receivers even when they weren’t open. And just like he used to do so often as a rookie, Daniels reminded everyone he has the clutch gene and made the big play when it mattered most. 2.J.J. McCarthy Hasn’t Made His Case Yet To Be The Giants Franchise Quarterback J.J. McCarthy has been mostly outstanding since the Giants acquired him from the Minnesota Vikings. He was terrific, for the most part, again on Thursday night. But if he wants to make the Giants even think about choosing him over Jaxson Dart as their quarterback next season, he can’t afford to lose too many more games like this. It wasn’t even about his game-ending interception. That was thrown out of desperation. It had more to do with the fact that even though he completed 22 of 36 passes for 294 yards and ran for 34 more yards, the offense shut down under his direction late in the fourth quarter when they could have put the game away. The Giants gave the Commanders life with two three-and-outs in the final 5.5 minutes. That just won’t do. The Giants are thrilled with McCarthy. They love his mobility. They're enthralled with his arm strength, as he showed in the fourth quarter with a bullet through double coverage to TE Isaiah Likely, which became a go-ahead, 66-yard touchdown pass. He’s doing most of everything they want. But he’s got a huge opportunity. The Giants have two 23-year-old potential franchise quarterbacks who will be under contract next season. They are committed to Dart, but they can just as easily change their commitment to McCarthy. McCarthy will just have to do a lot more than he did on Thursday night to earn it. 3.The Giants Don’t Have A Championship Defense The Giants’ top priority at the trade deadline was finding a defensive tackle who could not only help their leaky run defense, but also help them do the one thing they haven’t been able to do consistently since they lost edge rusher Brian Burns early in the season — pressure the quarterback. Their inability to do that cost them dearly against Daniels on Thursday night, and it’s really going to hurt them as they play better teams and quarterbacks down the stretch and maybe into the postseason. For most of the game, they couldn’t touch Daniels. Granted, he’s as elusive a quarterback as there is in the league, but the Giants made it easy on him. When he stayed in the pocket, he had plenty of time. When he escaped the pocket, it wasn’t because he was rushed, and there was nobody containing him on the outside. As a result, he picked them apart with his arm, after picking them apart with his legs in a 27-27 tie last month. The Giants rank near the bottom in the NFL with 17 sacks. They came into this game with a league-worst pressure rate of 18.9%. They’ve got Trevor Lawrence (Jacksonville), Brock Purdy (San Francisco), Jared Goff (Detroit) and Dak Prescott (Dallas) coming up over their next seven games. It’s great that they’re opportunistic. They have a very strong secondary. And they had two more interceptions on Thursday night. But the defense is really going to have to dial up the pressure against some of the NFL’s best quarterbacks to have a chance to survive. 3 ½. What's Next? It’s hard to overstate how much the Giants needed to pad their lead in the NFC East race on Thursday night, because this game marked the end point of the easy part of their schedule. Up next for them is a minefield of the NFL’s elite, starting with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 10 days. And they’ll also face the San Francisco 49ers, the Seattle Seahawks, the Cleveland Browns and the Detroit Lions over the next seven weeks. They are not quite in that class yet. And that could be a problem with the Cowboys now nipping at their heels. As for the Commanders, they now have new life in the division race. They have a tough game against the Cincinnati Bengals when they return, but after that they have a very winnable two-game road trip to Arizona and Tennessee, where they’ll face two of the worst teams in the league. That is a huge opportunity for them to make up some lost ground, and maybe really get into the thick of the race by the time they get to December.

articles.title: Javier Rodríguez Piris: "Queremos el Mundial de pádel 2030 en España"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la FEP visita MARCA con las copas de campeones del mundo
articles.summary: El presidente de la FEP visita MARCA con las copas de campeones del mundo
articles.body: Apenas han pasado unos días desde que España levantase en Doha (Qatar) la Copa de campeón del mundo de pádel por partida doble. Las chicas lograron el décimo campeonato y los chicos, el quinto, ambos tumbando a la otra gran potencia de este deporte: Argentina. Los dos trofeos visitaron ayer la redacción de MARCA con Javier Rodríguez Piris, presidente de la Federación Española de Pádel, a la cabeza. Orgulloso de lo logrado y aún con el subidón del éxito, ha sido recibido por el director adjunto, Emilio Contreras, y por el equipo de MARCA Pádel, donde ha repasado los éxitos logrados recientemente y también su etapa como mandatario cuando está a punto de cumplir un año. Pregunta: ¿Cómo se siente un bicampeón del mundo? Respuesta: La verdad es que estamos muy contentos. Ha sido una semana muy emocionante. Después de preparar todo el Mundial durante las semanas anteriores y de vivir toda la competición, traernos los dos campeonatos, las dos Copas del Mundo, nos hace estar muy, muy contentos. Pregunta: ¿Qué supone para una federación lograr los dos títulos más grandes que se pueden conseguir a nivel de selecciones? Es un inicio de mandato impresionante. Respuesta: Sí, la verdad es que llevamos casi un año y hemos tenido los Europeos de Menores, en los que hemos sido campeones, y la verdad es que está siendo un buen periodo. Ahora, ser campeones del mundo tanto en categoría masculina como femenina es un activo muy importante para nosotros y para la Federación. Es un orgullo poder sacar pecho y decir que somos España y que somos los mejores. Pregunta: ¿Cómo ha vivido la semana en Doha? Respuesta: La verdad es que ha sido una semana maravillosa. Tengo un recuerdo genial porque hemos convivido con todo el equipo y con toda la expedición oficial. Llevábamos dos delegados, que eran el vicepresidente primero y el segundo, el de Económico y el de Competición, Pepe y Paco. También llevábamos a los 16 deportistas, a los seleccionadores, Juanjo y Carolina, y a dos técnicos. Además, teníamos un jefe y un técnico de la URI, Guti, que han hecho un trabajo extraordinario. Han sido dos piezas clave. Después estaba el equipo de comunicación, con Nacho como director de Comunicación, Laura, Edu y Guillermo. También llevábamos a los dos fisioterapeutas. El lunes me reuní con toda la expedición y les dije que éramos un equipo, que cada uno tenía su función y que todos sabíamos lo que teníamos que hacer. Al final, se trataba de engranar toda esa maquinaria para conseguir las dos Copas del Mundo. Pregunta: ¿Cómo vivió el día de las finales? Respuesta: En principio, todo el mundo veía la final femenina bastante fácil para España, pero el partido se nos complicó en el encuentro que estaban disputando Paula y Gemma. Aunque en ningún momento vimos que peligrase la eliminatoria, nos fuimos al tercer set y empezaron los nervios. Empiezas a pensar que la cosa se puede complicar, pero al final salió bien. Después llegó el tema tan polémico de la alineación de Juanjo. En el primer partido todo el mundo estaba muy nervioso. Mirábamos las redes sociales y todo el mundo opinaba de todo. Luego está lo de Goñi, que fue extraordinario, y él es un encanto, un fenómeno. Había estado muy nervioso, pero al final Juan hizo un torneo y una semana maravillosos. Hizo un partidazo y Juanjo también los dirigió muy bien. El resto del equipo estuvo ahí, animando a tope, igual que las chicas. Pregunta: Presidente, ¿qué pensó cuando vio la alineación masculina? Respuesta: Honestamente, te digo que no me sorprendió tanto. Cuando viajé, yo estuve en Kuwait y dos días después viajamos juntos toda la expedición. Estuve hablando con los jugadores y les escuchaba. Notaba y me transmitían que estaban muy unidos, que eran un equipo. Comentaban las cosas que querían hacer y se les veía muy enchufados. Se lo dije en la reunión: 'Tengo buenas sensaciones'. Me estaba transmitiendo algo positivo y eso a veces se palpa. Tienes unas sensaciones que van más allá de lo que puedan decir los jugadores. Durante el partido, evidentemente, el resultado era complicado, pero siempre quedaba esa esperanza. Viendo cómo se estaban comportando y cómo estaba Juan, que en ningún momento dejó de luchar, de animar a Aimar, a Juanjo y a sus compañeros, había un ambiente especial. Además, esto es pádel. Como todos sabemos, puedes ganar un set por 6-0 y perder los otros dos también por 6-0. Al final, yo siempre tuve esperanza. Pregunta: Antes de todo el revuelo que se generó en las redes sociales, entiendo que la Federación Española está muy satisfecha con el trabajo de Juanjo Gutiérrez. Respuesta: Sí, la verdad es que Juanjo ha sabido manejar muy bien al grupo. Desde el principio, cuando acabamos en Kuwait, ya se vio su forma de trabajar. Estuvimos en la academia de Rafa Nadal, que está en Manacor, y allí se llevaron a cabo dinámicas de grupo con los jugadores. La verdad es que muy bien. Maneja muy bien el grupo. Yo nunca había estado en una concentración de este tipo con jugadores de este nivel y Juanjo sabe gestionar muy bien a los deportistas. Ha hecho una apuesta muy arriesgada y muchas veces, en esta vida, los campeones y los ganadores tienen que hacer apuestas arriesgadas. Pregunta: ¿Cree que estamos ante la mejor generación del pádel español de toda su historia? Respuesta: Yo creo que tenemos una generación femenina impresionante y en categoría masculina también contamos con algunos de los mejores jugadores. Siempre que me entrevistan digo lo mismo: tenemos a los mejores. En España tenemos lo mejor de todo el pádel: los mejores jugadores, los mejores técnicos, las mejores federaciones, los mejores gestores de federaciones, árbitros y clubes. Somos un ejemplo. En el Mundial se acercaba mucha gente y nos pedía consejo sobre determinadas cuestiones. Nuestra expedición era muy grande y el equipo de comunicación trabajó muy bien. Pregunta: ¿Por qué España es una de las principales potencias mundiales del pádel? Respuesta: Creo que se ha trabajado muy bien la base y desde la Federación estamos apostando por ello. En España ha habido técnicos muy buenos y gente que ha trabajado y sigue trabajando muy bien en las federaciones territoriales. Este es un éxito de las federaciones. Lo digo porque, sin el trabajo que hacen en formación, en sus campeonatos y en sus pruebas, esto no sería posible. Llevan muchos años trabajando muy bien y creo que otros países que están empezando deberían fijarse en cómo lo tenemos organizado en España. El trabajo de las federaciones territoriales con sus campeonatos es fundamental. A los jugadores también se lo dije en aquella charla: más allá de vuestro talento y de vuestro esfuerzo, que evidentemente sois grandes jugadores, ha habido una federación y una persona que se ha encargado de organizar un torneo, de preparar un campeonato y de conseguir que os animéis a jugar. Todo eso ha contribuido a que hoy estéis donde estáis. Siempre hay que pensar un poco de dónde se viene. En este caso, detrás están las federaciones territoriales, los técnicos, los organizadores, los presidentes de las territoriales, los gerentes y los árbitros. Somos un ecosistema de pádel muy importante. Pregunta: ¿Están otros países siguiendo ese camino de trabajo que está marcando España, desde la base hasta el profesionalismo? Respuesta: Sí, se está trabajando muy bien. En el Europeo de Menores de Oporto, por ejemplo, la final júnior fue contra Francia. Nos hicieron un set y estaban jugando Coquito y Iago, que forman una pareja muy buena. Había chicos de mucho nivel. También podemos ver que Italia, en categoría femenina, siempre está ahí. Ya quedó tercera en el anterior Mundial. Además, tenemos a Iciar Montes, que ha sido seleccionadora nuestra y que ahora está en Gran Bretaña, donde hay escuelas y jugadores españoles que están trabajando muy bien. También está Willy Lahoz, con quien estuvimos en Emiratos Árabes. Hay mucha gente trabajando fuera y la marca España está teniendo una influencia muy importante. En Europa, países como Países Bajos, Suecia y Portugal están trabajando muy bien. Los portugueses, por ejemplo, quedaron terceros en categoría masculina. Jugamos contra ellos en semifinales y tienen un buen equipo. Están haciendo un gran trabajo. Sé que en Portugal están yendo equipos desde Extremadura para trabajar allí, con técnicos y escuelas de competición que están desarrollando una labor muy interesante. Pregunta: ¿España ha dejado de crecer y está llegando a un grado de madurez o, como presidente de la Federación Española, considera que todavía hay margen de crecimiento? Respuesta: Yo te diría que se está produciendo una profesionalización cada vez mayor. Se está dando un salto importante en los clubes. Por ejemplo, en los clubes que conozco veo que antes se montaba uno en cualquier nave, con cuatro pistas, y poco más. Ahora los clubes que se están construyendo son grandes instalaciones profesionales, con un buen gimnasio, un buen sistema de servicios, cafetería e incluso residencias para alojar deportistas. Se está dando un salto importante. Después, a nivel de menores, también se está trabajando muy bien. Los técnicos están creando escuelas de competición importantes y hay que seguir en esa línea porque, como estamos comentando, vienen muchos países y los estamos viendo por el retrovisor. Ese es nuestro objetivo: trabajar mucho el pádel de base y la formación. También vamos a hacer cambios en 2027 en el ámbito formativo, porque cualquier organización que quiera progresar y crecer tiene que contar con un buen sistema de formación. Pregunta: ¿Cuáles son los objetivos generales que se marcó cuando llegaste a la presidencia, hace poco menos de un año? Respuesta: Yo me encontré una federación totalmente desestructurada. No voy a entrar en ejemplos concretos, pero había una falta de organización y de comunicación tremenda. Prácticamente no había nadie. Yo llegué el 23 de diciembre. Había sido elegido por la Asamblea el día 18 y, cinco días hábiles después, entró en vigor la resolución de mi nombramiento. Tenía que subir una noticia anunciando que era el nuevo presidente y tuve que redactarla, pegarla, colocarla, hacer un PDF y llamar al informático para que la subiera. Imagínate cómo estaba aquello. Además, veníamos de un proceso electoral largo, en el que hubo problemas entre varias candidaturas, y estaba todo bastante dejado de la mano. Creo que el anterior presidente llegó a un momento en el que pensó que aquello se quedase como estaba. Así que había que hacer una reestructuración completa. Pregunta: ¿Cómo es la relación actual con la Federación Internacional de Pádel? Respuesta: La verdad es que tenemos una relación buena y muy cordial. Con el presidente, Luigi Carraro, tengo muy buena relación. Al principio, cuando llegamos, había una serie de cuestiones con las que no estábamos de acuerdo, especialmente en cómo se estaban organizando las competiciones de CUPRA FIP Tour y los problemas que se habían generado posteriormente con los torneos de Premier Padel. No había un orden ni una coordinación con la Federación Española. Fue una de las primeras cosas que hablamos. Vimos que había que coordinar y regular las competiciones entre ambas partes para evitar que nos pisáramos. No podía celebrarse un CUPRA FIP Tour Bronce al mismo tiempo que un campeonato en una comunidad autónoma cercana, o que coincidieran un campeonato de menores y un torneo de Premier Padel en Santander y otro en Extremadura. En el resto de cuestiones, muy bien. El día 12 de octubre celebramos la Asamblea en Madrid, en el COE, y fue genial. Tenemos muy buena relación con Alejandro Blanco, presidente del Comité Olímpico Español, y su apoyo es muy importante para que el pádel pueda ser olímpico algún día, que es lo que todos queremos. Pregunta. Los Juegos Olímpicos. Siendo realistas, Javier, ¿cuándo cree que podría llegar la entrada del pádel en el programa olímpico? Respuesta: Ahora hay una oportunidad importante. Como comentaba, el presidente del Comité Olímpico Español, Alejandro Blanco, se presenta como candidato a la presidencia de ANOC. Las elecciones serán los días 6 y 7 de diciembre y sería un paso muy importante. Ojalá pudiera llegar para 2032, aunque quizá sea pronto. Si no, creo que para 2036 podría ser olímpico. El pádel cumple con creces muchos de los requisitos que se exigen: está presente en muchos países, hay muchísima gente que lo practica y existe un desarrollo importante. Se están haciendo muchas cosas y hemos participado en los Juegos del Mediterráneo. Estamos avanzando en hitos importantes dentro de todo el movimiento olímpico. Ojalá sea en 2032 y, si no, en 2036. Creo que es posible, la verdad. Pregunta: ¿Qué cosas tiene ahora mismo entre ceja y ceja para cambiar o modificar? Respuesta: Por ejemplo, me gustaría trabajar más en el crecimiento de las licencias federativas. Hemos acabado 2025 con 117.500 licencias. Se calcula que practican pádel unos cuatro millones de personas en España. Esta misma mañana estábamos ya cerca de las 120.000 licencias y las hemos superado. No sé si hemos llegado a un pico que no vamos a poder superar, pero creo que deberíamos trabajar más para que la gente se federe, compita con un seguro y esté respaldada por una estructura que permita tener un control. Hay muchas ligas que se organizan y que no están respaldadas por nada. Necesitamos saber exactamente cuánta gente juega al pádel y cómo se juega. Todo debería estar bajo el paraguas de las federaciones, porque cuanto más estructurado, regulado y controlado esté el deporte, mejor. Para mí es algo muy importante porque creo que podemos crecer mucho. Tenemos por delante al fútbol y al baloncesto, pero después ya estamos por encima del resto de deportes en número de licencias. Pregunta: ¿Cómo se puede acerca al practicante habitual de pádel que no consume pádel profesional a, precisamente, que lo consuma? Respuesta: Dándole visibilidad. Es lo que estamos intentando hacer hoy y lo que intentamos hacer siempre: traer campeonatos y pruebas a España. Yo siempre lo digo: me gustaría que en España hubiera un torneo Major y, por qué no, que en 2030 pudiéramos organizar un Mundial. Sería impresionante. Creo que España está muy preparada. En nuestro país se organizan pruebas de Fórmula 1 y de muchos otros deportes a unos niveles extraordinarios. Por eso, creo que la forma de acercar el pádel a la gente es conseguir que lo vea y que lo sienta más cerca. Hay que darle mucha visibilidad. Ya planteé esta cuestión en la última presentación del P1 de Madrid. Lo comenté y también lo he hablado con el presidente de la Federación Internacional. Si en algún momento el Major se trasladase a otro sitio, podría abrirse la posibilidad de organizar un Mundial aquí, porque hay muchos países interesados en acoger pruebas. Estuve con el presidente de Japón y también quieren organizar una competición en China. En todos los sitios quieren llevarse pruebas. El pádel está creciendo muchísimo en Asia y cualquier día podríamos encontrarnos con el anuncio de un torneo de Premier Padel en China, Japón o algún otro país. Pregunta: ¿Ve factible entonces que España pueda organizar un Mundial? Respuesta: Estamos preparadísimos. Creo que tendría una difusión enorme y que España está preparada. Este país está preparado para organizar cualquier tipo de evento de esas características si se planifica con tiempo. Sería increíble, impresionante. Intentaremos trabajarlo ahora que tenemos tiempo. El Mundial de 2028 ya está previsto que se celebre en Qatar, así que tenemos margen para trabajar, hablar y ver si alguna institución se presta a organizarlo. P. Habría dos mundiales en 2030 en España. R. Sería impresionante. Evidentemente, organizar un Mundial tiene un coste elevado, pero creo que sería una buena inversión y tendría un retorno muy importante.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels throws three touchdowns as Commanders rally past Giants Thursday night
articles.summary: Malik Nabers and the New York Giants fell 24-21 as Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns to rally the Washington Commanders in a key NFC East clash.
articles.body: Taking a cue from coach John Harbaugh’s stated goal of going 1-0 each week, Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers viewed Thursday night’s rematch with Washington as carrying extra weight after the teams tied last month in Week 5. The Week 10 matchup was never tied, and Washington ultimately won 24-21, giving the Commanders a much-needed victory over their NFC East rival. J.J. McCarthy made his first home start since joining the Giants in a late-September trade from Minnesota. articles.title: Harry Kane breaks caps record as England reach Nations League knockouts
articles.summary: England moved to second spot in Group A3 behind Spain, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.
articles.body:
Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England cap with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarterfinals.

Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid another embarrassment after their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kickoff at Wembley.

But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in Group A3 behind Spain, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.

Thomas Tuchel’s men have a chance to avenge their 3-2 defeat against the world champions in their Nations League opener when they travel to Madrid for Sunday’s clash.

Spain beat Czechia 2-0 in Prague on Thursday.

“After the first game when we lost here against them [Spain], we knew we left a bit out there,” Kane told ITV.

“We knew we could’ve done a bit better. We said to ourselves, ‘Let’s win every game until the next one and see what happens’. It’s the perfect opportunity now on Sunday to try and prove ourselves.”

England and Croatia struggled to get out of second gear in the opening stages of their match in London.

Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute, and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.

Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion, following a neat move by the home side.

Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball the first time across the area towards Rogers.

Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.

England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time.

The home side were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period.

But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner.

The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home.

Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area.

Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty, but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot.

Kane made no mistake, drilling home for a record-extending 92nd England goal.

Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive.

James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back, but Bellingham was in an offside position when he received the ball.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off, taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

A giant banner was raised before kickoff with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

articles.title: Ukraine war: Finland, Norway block visas for Russian athletes
articles.summary: Finland and Norway have announced fresh restrictions on Russian athletes, making it difficult for them to compete in the two Nordic countries as the war
articles.body: Finland and Norway have announced fresh restrictions on Russian athletes, making it difficult for them to compete in the two Nordic countries as the war in Ukraine continues.Finland announced on Thursday that it would restrict visas for Russian athletes, saying they had "no business" in the country as long as the war continued. Hours later, Norway said it would stop professional Russian and Belarusian sportspersons from competing on its soil.The decisions could affect major international sporting events scheduled in both countries.Finland says Russian athletes have 'no business' in countryFinland has tightened rules for Russian citizens applying for short-term work visas, including those seeking to take part in professional sports.Under the new rules, "Russian citizens will only be allowed to work under a Schengen visa in tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests," the Finnish foreign ministry said in a statement.The restrictions will also apply to Russian athletes competing under a neutral flag. They will not be allowed to obtain visas to enter Finland."As long as Russia's war of aggression continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland," Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said in a statement."Their entry into the country would be a threat to Finland's international relations."The new rules will come into effect on November 16. Finland shares a 1,340-kilometre (830-mile) border with Russia.The country is scheduled to host the Figure Skating World Championships in Tampere in March 2027. The International Skating Union (ISU) said it was "studying" the possible impact of Finland's decision."The aim of the change is to prevent entries that Russia could use to spread messages supporting its war," Valtonen told reporters.Russia uses "sports as a tool for propaganda", she added.Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga welcomed Finland's move. In a post on X, he urged other European countries to "close the remaining loopholes, and strengthen coordinated pressure on Russia,".Norway also blocks Russian and Belarusian athletesNorway announced its decision a few hours after Finland. Its government said the country already had strict visa rules for Russian and Belarusian citizens.However, recent "relaxations introduced by international sports federations" could allow more athletes and support staff from the two countries to travel to Norway for competitions.The new decision could prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes from competing even if they have been cleared by the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS).Norway is preparing to host the Cross-Country Skiing World Cup in Trondheim in December.ISU questions Finland's decisionThe ISU said it believed athletes should not be held responsible for the actions of their governments. It said "that athletes should not be punished for the actions of the governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing".The governing body added that it was seeking "further clarifications" from the Finnish organisers.CAS ruling brings Russian ice hockey team back into focusFinland's decision comes after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on October 30 opened the possibility of the Russian ice hockey team returning to the World Championships next year. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), which has banned Russia from competitions since its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, had opposed the CAS decision.Several countries, including Finland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic, have said they would refuse to play against Russia at the World Championships in Germany.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also said last week that Russia would not be allowed to compete at the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championships in Alberta. The Finnish city of Turku has announced that it will withdraw from hosting the 2027-28 edition of the tournament if Russia takes part.Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin last week praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for "taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles". He also criticised countries that are opposing Russia's return to international sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia captain Pat Cummins denies involvement in ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal
articles.summary: Cummins says Khawaja was ‘100 percent wrong’ in claiming the whole team knew about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
articles.body:
Australia captain Pat Cummins ⁠has again denied any involvement in ⁠the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in a Test against South Africa in 2018, describing the allegations in Usman Khawaja’s autobiography as “utter nonsense”.

Former Australia batsman Khawaja, whose autobiography was published on Tuesday, said last weekend that all the players in the team knew about ⁠the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing. His latest comments triggered calls for a new investigation into the incident.

The scandal centred around the third Test in Cape Town, but Khawaja also claimed the tactic was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth.

“When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he’s 100 percent wrong. I’ve said that consistently for the last eight years,” Cummins told a news conference in Sydney on Friday.

“I did not know that was happening, but I think ⁠Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that.

“He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That’s complete and utter nonsense.

“There was no master plan around using illegal methods,” he added. “There’s no grand plan. There’s no team meeting. There’s no bowlers saying ‘this is what must happen’.”

Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan.

Darren Lehmann, who was the Australian head coach at the time, has also denied any knowledge, as has former batting coach Graeme Hick, who called Khawaja’s allegations “absolutely false”.

Cummins spoke for 68 minutes on Friday, taking every question from the media and saying he would never discuss the ball-tampering incident again.

The Australia skipper also took exception to Pakistan-born Khawaja’s contention in the book that the colour of his ‌skin and background had prevented him from becoming Australia captain.

“I think of all the things that I’ve read this week, I think that’s actually the most serious,” he said.

“Him saying that if you’re Australian captain, you have to be a certain skin colour, I couldn’t disagree with that statement any more.”

Steve Smith and David Warner, the then-Australia captain and vice-captain, were banned by Cricket Australia from elite cricket for a year for their roles in the ball-tampering.

Opening batter Cameron Bancroft, who brought a piece of sandpaper onto the field, received a nine-month suspension for his part in the ball-tampering.

“I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam to be careful when using sandpaper. That’s not the Usman that I know,” Cummins said.

“It’s not the Usman that has helped rebuild the Australian cricket ⁠culture over the last eight years.”

Later on Friday, Warner said the trio had paid a heavy price for the incident and revealed ⁠that his wife Candice had lost a baby in the aftermath of what became known as “ Sandpapergate “.

“I still stick by Uzzie and what he has written in that book. It is the truth,” the former Test opener said in TV commentary ahead of a one-day international between Australia and England.

“I actually feel for [Khawaja] at the moment. I actually feel that the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus and I’m very disappointed ⁠by that.”

Cummins was asked about Khawaja’s recollection that two players had rejected the batsman’s call for the team to take collective responsibility for the ball-tampering.

“I don’t remember any conversation around collective responsibility,” he said.

“So then, I’ve got no idea who ⁠those two people would be because I don’t remember ever being asked or having a conversation about it.”

Khawaja and ⁠Warner have also been critical of the Cricket Australia investigation in 2018 that found the three punished players solely responsible for the plot.

“I got asked to be part of that review,” Cummins said. “I was totally truthful. I’ve been very consistent since then at that event till now. Nothing’s changed.”

Earlier this week, the head of Cricket Australia ruled out opening another investigation into the 2018 incident.

Cummins said he respected the right of Khawaja to tell ‌his story in the autobiography but felt some of the allegations were very serious and had to be addressed.

“Usman’s a friend, but friends aren’t casual with each other’s lives and reputations,” he said.

“In his book, Uzzie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket.”

Cummins added, though, that he would not ‌be ‌taking legal action against Khawaja over the allegations in the book.

“I did get advised this week that some of the things that’ve been said are probably defamatory, but I won’t be doing that,” Cummins said.

“You’ve got to move on. It’s been eight years. We’re moving on. So, you got to draw a line at some point.”

articles.title: Ballon d’Or dream: 11-year-old footballer Riaan hopes to play for Real Madrid
articles.summary: At just 11, Indian footballer Riaan Ghodawat has already experienced something that many young players can only dream of.
articles.body: At just 11, Indian footballer Riaan Ghodawat has already experienced something that many young players can only dream of. On October 26, 2026, he became the first Indian to attend the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, where he got a chance to be around some of the biggest names in world football.A member of the Real Madrid Academy India, Riaan has already had several opportunities to experience football at the international level. He has attended training camps organised by Paris Saint-Germain and West Ham United in London. He has also competed at the Real Madrid World Championship in Madrid and the Singa Cup in Singapore.He has also travelled to Barcelona to watch El Clásico between Real Madrid and Barcelona. His progress has attracted interest from clubs in the UK, and he has received offers to join them.A dream evening at the Ballon d’OrThe Ballon d’Or ceremony gave Riaan a chance to see football from a different perspective. Instead of being on the training ground or playing a match, he was in a room with some of the sport's biggest names as their achievements were celebrated.“When I found out I was going to the Ballon d’Or, I could not stop smiling,” said Riaan. “I have watched these players on screen and followed their journeys. Being in the same room as them was something I had never imagined. It made me want to work even harder at my football.”Wants to play for Barcelona or Real MadridRiaan's main focus remains on becoming a professional footballer. He dreams of playing for either FC Barcelona or Real Madrid. Attending the Ballon d’Or has given him another goal to work towards — returning to the ceremony one day as a player.“I want to play for FC Barcelona or Real Madrid and return to the Ballon d’Or as a player,” he said. “For now, I know I have a lot to learn, and I want to keep training and getting better.”For the young footballer, the evening in London was an important moment in a journey that has only just begun. articles.title: Legendary coach Terry Waters finds new role at Fishburne
articles.summary: After 49 years of coaching, Hall of Famer Terry Waters is transitioning to athletic director at Fishburne.
articles.body:
WAYNESBORO — Terry Waters is a legendary wrestling coach in the area.

He was inducted into the Virginia Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2022, and his photo and biographical info are in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in Stillwater, Oklahoma. Most assumed he would coach wrestling until he retired and then just walk away.

Raised in a hot bed of wrestling in Pennsylvania, Waters was a student at Milton Hershey School, a boarding school for low-income families in Hershey. He and his brother were among the first Black students at the school after it integrated.

Locally, Waters has coached at Staunton, Riverheads and Fort Defiance high schools, as well as at Washington & Lee University, where he was an assistant. He came to Fishburne in 2015.

This past summer, he announced he was retiring from coaching. It seemed to be the end of an amazing career, but then he announced, not too longer afterward, that he would be staying at the Waynesboro school to serve as athletic director.

He's now through the fall season and about to start winter sports.

"It hasn't gone totally smooth, but it's been a great transition," Waters said. "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids."

He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging.

"You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually."

Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be.

"I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well."

Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued.

"When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open."

Every year, at least in recent years, someone would ask the veteran coach how much longer. His answer was always one more year. He'd talk with his wife about his future in coaching after the season ended. She would tell him if he still had the energy and the desire, he should keep coaching.

"My brother pretty much summed it up when he told me if you like what you're doing, there is no sense in retiring," he said.

But this summer, he clearly remembers waking up one morning and thinking, "I'm done." He told the Fishburne staff about his decision. He was planning to just walk away, but then the athletic director position opened. Waters decided to apply.

"I've had athletic directors across the state send me notes telling me if I needed any help just let them know," Waters said. He said Frank Kahrs at Grace Christian has been particularly helpful. He's also talked with Staunton's David Tibbs about some questions he had. All the connections Waters has built over the years are proving to be helpful in the new job.

"I believe I'm here because it's where God wants me," Waters said.

The day-to-day life of an athletics director is never the same, and never boring, Waters said.

"You spend a lot more time than I actually though on the computer," he said, "sending emails out, setting schedules, things like that."

It's about a 10-hour a day job, give or take, and Waters said he's fine with that. He does have two assistant athletic directors that help take some of the burden off of him, but Waters said he'll be at every home event at Fishburne. He feels it's his responsibility.

Wrestling this winter may be the toughest for him because he's not coaching — although, maybe not.

"I don't think I'm going to miss it as much as other people think I'm going to miss it," Waters said. "I just want to make sure I don't step on toes."

Rick Palmer is taking over as head wrestling coach at Fishburne. Waters said he has confidence in Palmer's abilities to continue leading the program. Still, Waters said home wrestling events will be difficult, sitting in the stands watching instead of in the corner of the mat coaching.

"That is something that will be hard," he said, "but I'm prepared for that. I've done all I want to do in coaching in 49 years. I don't have anything else to prove. I was ready to step down. I was comfortable in my decision."

articles.title: 6 takeaways from Commanders' TNF win over Giants
articles.summary: Six takeaways from the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders got a much-needed win on Thursday, defeating the New York Giants 24-21 to improve to 3-5-1.

It wasn't easy, as the two teams traded the lead throughout the game. It looked like the Giants were about to put it away late in the fourth quarter when Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels threw his second interception of the year — on back-to-back possessions. However, the defense kept getting stops when it mattered; Daniels found redemption with a game-winning touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs.

Washington's defense won it when cornerback Rasul Douglas picked off JJ McCarthy.

Here are six takeaways from a huge Commanders' win.

We know about Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs and Sonny Styles, but Washington was also helped by several others. Ben Sinnott had a career night, catching four passes for 46 yards and a touchdown and showing what he can do with more opportunities. Safety Jeremy Reaves has quietly had a really good year. Reaves was everywhere on Thursday, hitting JJ McCarthy and in coverage. He also recovered a fumble. Reaves also finished with nine tackles. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler didn't put up big numbers, but had some tough runs. Nick Allegretti returned to the starting lineup and played well. How about Luke McCaffrey's heads-up play on the kickoff return on the final possession? Huge play. A true team win for Washington.

Jayden Daniels has battled a lot of adversity the last two years. This year, there was the elbow injury, the late-game shenanigans against the Giants in Week 5 and coming up just short against the Rams and 49ers in recent weeks. But the one thing he hadn't done was throw an interception. On Thursday, he picked a bad time to throw his first — and his second — interception. They came on back-to-back possessions. But fortunately, the defense bailed him out. Daniels, like any great quarterback, has a short memory. He led the Commanders on a game-winning drive, beating the pressure to find Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown. There has been a lot of talk about whether Daniels takes enough chances. It's foolish talk. He takes chances; he's just excellent at protecting the ball. He slipped up on Thursday, and his teammates had his back. He had theirs, too. Daniels needed a win like that. So did his team.

Things looked bleak for a moment when JJ McCarthy found Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown to put the Giants back up 21-17. What made it frustrating was that defensive coordinator Daronte Jones called the perfect blitz on third-and-7. However, safety Nick Cross let up, allowing McCarthy to get a throw off. Had Cross simply kept going or put his hands up, that play would never have happened, and the Commanders would have gotten off the field. It would be interesting to hear from Cross about why he hesitated. He once again played a terrific game, but that's probably one he'd like to have back. Ultimately, it didn't cost him.

Washington came into the game as the worst team on third downs. Against a good New York defense, the Commanders converted on 7 of 14 third downs. It was a combination of Daniels throwing the ball, smart playcalling, clutch short-yardage runs and Daniels using his legs. Everything worked. Washington's third-down performance was one of the primary reasons it won on Thursday.

We still aren't sure what Daronte Jones' future is in Washington. But in the last few weeks, he certainly looks like a keeper. The defense is playing much better. He's aggressive, and players are getting better each week under his watch. We've witnessed far too many times over the years a Washington defensive coordinator play it safe late. They get burned almost every time. Jones wasn't having it. On three straight plays, he went after McCarthy. All three plays went in the Commanders' favor, with the final one being a Rasul Douglas game-winning interception. A terrific night for Jones and offensive coordinator David Blough. Even more impressive, it was on a short week.

The last time the Commanders and Giants played, New York came after Daniels every time he dropped back. While they didn't pressure as often on Thursday, they tried, and the Commanders' offensive line shut them down. Nick Allegretti was back in the lineup at center and played well. No snap issues. He also didn't allow a single pressure. The interior of the offensive line — outside of Sam Cosmi — has been criticized often this season. For good reason. On Thursday, they stepped up, cut down on the pre-snap penalties and looked much better than they did five weeks ago. Daniels was sacked only once and had a clean pocket for most of his attempts.

articles.title: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team
articles.summary: All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is made up of members of the area programs and includes Coach of the Year Ken Delaney of Coldwater.
articles.body:
BATTLE CREEK - Never losing a game from late August until October. Winning a conference title and a district crown.

For helping his team accomplish all of that, Coldwater's Ken Delaney is the 2026 All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team Coach of the Year.

The All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is selected by nominations from the city and area coaches and voted on by the Enquirer sports staff.

In his 18th season as head coach, Delaney is on a roll with state-ranked teams in back-to-back years as the Cardinals were 15-2-2 overall. Coldwater finished as Interstate 8 Conference champs with a 6-0 record in the league and won a second district title in the last three years. Along the way, Coldwater went unbeaten from August 20 until the regionals and climbed to as high as No. 12 in the Michigan Interscholastic High School Soccer Coaches rankings in Division 2.

Delaney is joined on the All-Enquirer team by Cardinals players Abdulhamid Munassar, Ahmen Norman, Riath Shamaala and Jensely Norvilus.

Lakeview finished as All-City Tournament champs and adds Mang Sung, Richard Lian and Cristian Duran to the team.

Harper Creek had the most wins in program history as Beavers' Jake Cushman, Broderick Hanger and TJ Ruble were named All-Enquirer.

Also from the city, earning All-Enquirer honors, are Pennfield's Philipp Kruetz and Everett Wilkins, Battle Creek Central's Yoani Bautista Trejo and Deangelo Crape, with the St. Philip/Calhoun co-op program adding Ashton Heighton and Ben Kaczanowski.

Among area teams, Marshall's Brandon Baker, Rowdy Joseph, Carson Clapper and Trenton Wolkiewicz were named as All-Enquirer members, as well as Gull Lake's Charlie Trantham, Ethan Waldorf.
