articles.title: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep
articles.summary: Panthers follow up rout of Mustangs with a tough win over Cougars in front of big crowd.
articles.body:
Just two weeks into the season and the Bloomington South girls basketball team has vanquished it's two county rivals.

The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. So it was a great early-season introduction to a sectional-like atmosphere for both teams in front of a vocal crowd at South on Thursday, Nov. 12.

Offense was hard to come by as the Panthers held off a second-half rally by North, getting a huge 3-pointer from freshman Quinn Wurtzman with 2:10 left in a five-point game to pull out a 48-37 win. It followed a much less rowdy 62-20 rout of Edgewood on Tuesday.

"We knew it was going to be a great crowd," North coach Kiley Jarrett said. "That's what we wanted. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was.

"I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference."

Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more.

"Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way.

"And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring."

South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line.

"We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens."

Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far.

"They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something.

"If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up."

South (2-1) will always lean on its defense, and forcing 11 turnovers in the first half led to some easy buckets and a 29-16 lead at the break. North had some key players in early foul trouble and the physical affects of the South press led to some 'tired' errors.

"It was just mistakes on our part," Jarrett said. "Foul trouble didn't help us at all, it got us out of our typical rotation."

But the Panthers' offensive struggles peaked in the third, going 2-of-11, forcing up some tough shots in the lane all night. That allowed the Cougars (0-2), who had just five more turnovers and played strong half-court defense most of the night, to chip away at the deficit.

"We know that when we play them that if we can keep them in the half-court and not turn the ball over, then we're going to be in good shape," Jarrett said.

North got within 33-27 at the end of three, but South wouldn't let them get any closer. A jump hook by Quinnly Fife and a banked in 3 by Avery Schwartzman from the top of the key while being fouled made it 38-29 with 6:26 to go.

But a 3 from Rilynn Williams, who had a game high 13 points, made it 40-35 with 2:40 left.

"She definitely is a more assertive player this year," Jarrett said. "And she stepped up tonight and made some huge plays for us. That 3 from the corner was absolutely huge. And I thought she did a good job defensively on Lehr."

But that's when Wurtzman took the next big shot of the night, knocking home a 3 from 22 feet to start an 8-0 run that put the game away.

"Knowing Quinn, she was ready for that shot and she'll be ready for that again," Jarrett said "It may say she's a freshman but she doesn't play like it and we knew that coming in.

"Credit to her. That was a momentum changer because I definitely felt like momentum was on our side before that."

All the same, Winters is looking at the big picture with his younger players.

"That was a big 3 but there were three layups she missed," Winters said. "If you're going to make the long one, make the short one. But that's the pressure of playing in your first North-South game."

South started the week with a 62-20 win at Edgewood, a game that got away quickly after the young Mustangs tied it at 8-8 with 1:40 left in the first quarter.

The Panthers scored the next 22 points as Edgewood coughed it up 20 times in the first half. It was 31-10 at the break and South put the running clock in motion late in the third, up 49-13.

Edgewood was limited to four field goals, just one inside the arc. The frustration was evident, but South is also likely the best team the Mustangs will see all season.

"You just have to harp on the positive things that we did," Edgewood coach Noah Stuckey said. "I feel like, that first quarter, we competed as well as we possibly could. We handled their physicality and got to the free throw line and then we just kinds of wore down.

"We got punched and wilted a little bit and didn't bring the energy in the second half."

It was just the second varsity team for the entire lineup so the speed and strength it takes to succeed at that level was on display.

On either side of that loss against the best team on their schedule, the Mustangs opened with a win over Greencastle 42-32 and then topped South Putnam 40-31 on Thursday.

"It felt awkward," Stuckey said of the win over Greencastle. "We started very strong, we got in some foul trouble and they made a run at us. Then, the second half, Kaitlyn (Ripley) took over. She didn't play the second quarter and had 23 points.

"The way they've been playing maybe the last couple of years is just stand and watch her," Stuckey said. "And we just can't rely on her to do everything. We've got to help her out and we kind of got in that run in the second and third quarter (against South)."

articles.title: Bears Stadium Bids Flood In As Developers Push City Plan
articles.summary: Developers pitch a $10 billion stadium plan for Chicago while the Bears eye Indiana. The city fights back with bold new offers.
articles.body:
Developers are flooding the market with unsolicited bids to keep the Chicago Bears in the city, but the team's focus remains on a suburban deal or a move to Indiana. This bid arrives as the Bears prepare for a legislative session in Illinois starting Nov. 17, yet the franchise has not endorsed any of these urban proposals.

The group plans to span about 100 acres and include a stadium for 75,000 fans alongside thousands of new homes. They argue that an urban site offers better economic value than remote suburbs. "It is our belief that a modern, competitive dome stadium such as the one that we are proposing will outperform suburban locations such as Arlington Heights or northwest Indiana," said Quintin Primo III, founder and executive chairman of Capri Investment Group, during a news conference in Bronzeville, according to Yahoo . Local leaders back the idea, but the NFL has previously flagged the specific Reese parcel as too narrow with active rail lines running through it.

While local boosters push for a downtown solution, the Bears are actively exploring a path across the state line. Nearly nine months ago, Indiana state leaders approved a funding package, and due diligence has been completed regarding two potential locations in Hammond. The team has not commented on the specific Chicago proposals but is watching the Illinois political process closely. "We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks," the Bears said last week regarding the two states, according to Yahoo Sports . The franchise is seeking property tax certainty and infrastructure help, with its main focus still on its own land in suburban Arlington Heights.

Capri's group is prepared to purchase the Bears' current Arlington Heights property, which would solve the land issue but force the team to abandon its preferred suburban setup. Chicago 4th Ward Alderman Lamont Robinson voiced strong support for the Bronzeville plan, stating it serves the community best. "I believe with everything I have, it's the right thing for the 4th ward. And the right thing for Chicago and the bears," Robinson said. The developers claim their plan will shape the city for generations, but the team holds the real power in the negotiation.

Newly reelected Gov. JB Pritzker intends to advance a Bears-related bill during the upcoming veto session, creating a critical moment for the stadium saga. The recent rise in developer activity suggests growing confidence that a bill could pass, even as the team keeps its Indiana option alive. The Reese option joins similar unsolicited offers made in recent weeks for sites at the former South Works steel mill and Rate Field. "We have an opportunity to make a decision that will shape Chicago for generations," said Quintin Primo III, Capri founder and executive chairman. The Bears must decide soon if they will stay in the city or leave for a new home.

Due diligence was completed on two potential locations in Hammond after Indiana state leaders approved a funding package nearly nine months ago.

articles.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI to provide welcome distraction to sandpaper scandal
articles.summary: England experienced more misery in Perth having thrown away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago
articles.body:
England crashed to a heavy defeat in the first game of their latest Australian tour, with a rousing debut from 21-year-old Mahli Beardman diverting some of the home side's attention from the ongoing sandpaper scandal .

Australian cricket is in the midst of a bitter civil war over Usman Khawaja's historic ball-tampering allegations but the hosts still eased to a seven-wicket victory in in the first ODI in Perth , where local boy Beardman collected stunning figures of six for 24.

It proved another calamitous visit to Optus Stadium for England, who thew away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago.

With Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood all rested between Test series, Australia pieced together an inexperienced attack and watched as it dismantled their rivals. At one stage England were 65 for eight and staring at a record low total, with some late repair work by the tail lifting them to 131 all out.

Travis Head missed the chance to repeat his match-winning Ashes knock when he was bowled cheaply by Gus Atkinson but skipper Mitch Marsh took up the mantle, clubbing 50 off just 30 balls to lead a chase that was all over in less than 24 overs.

England were criticised last winter for being too casual in their preparations Down Under but that has not been the case this time. They have trained hard, given themselves time to acclimatise and beaten Western Australia in a warm-up game at the WACA.

All of that work came to nothing, though, as they followed up a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan with a fourth loss in their last five outings.

After being sent in England's openers scraped together 24 before Australia bagged their first, Ben Duckett slashing Spencer Johnson to backward point.

Tom Banton came closer than anyone to finding form, hitting five fours on his way to 25 before driving with hard hands at the tidy Xavier Bartlett.

An average start then transformed into a dreadful once as the introduction of Beardman plunged the innings into turmoil.

Kicking off his senior international career with England's two best batters at the crease, the youngster got the best of both. His eighth ball was sharp and well directed, with enough swing to take the outside edge as Harry Brook went back in defence.

Joe Root , on the day he became just the third Englishman to 200 ODI appearances, was even bigger scalp. Muddling his way to 17 from 36 balls, he was put down by Cooper Connolly on three before an optimistic drive off Beardman wound up in Josh Inglis' gloves.

The celebrations showed how much that wicket meant but he was just warming up. Jordan Cox followed to another defensive nick and Beardman showed his range by bouncing out Sam Curran , who hooked obligingly to fine leg for a seven-ball duck. Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut.

England's woes continued as Jamie Overton 's ugly top-edge was plucked one-handed by the returning Johnson but Will Jacks ' 25 and Atkinson's punchy 29 not out saw them double their total.

Beardman returned to end the innings, dismissing Jofra Archer to claim record debut figures for Australia and match England's best ever analysis in the format, by Reece Topley in 2022.

Atkinson bowled Head with his first delivery but Australia never threatened to let the result slip. Marsh put his foot down, blazing four sixes and four fours, effectively settling the matter by the time flicked Overton to deep-midwicket in the ninth over.

Banton misjudged a steepling catch to spare Connolly on five, who added 22 more before poking Archer to gully.

Inglis and Matt Renshaw did the rest with minimal fuss, leaving 159 deliveries unused.

articles.title: Yorkshire re-sign paceman Ali on T20 deal
articles.summary: Yorkshire re-sign Pakistan fast bowler Hassan Ali on a two-year T20 Blast contract for 2027 and 2028.
articles.body:
Pakistan fast bowler Hassan Ali has signed a new two-year T20 Blast contract with Yorkshire for 2027 and 2028.

The former Warwickshire paceman has committed himself to a sixth successive summer playing in the Blast following his initial arrival in English cricket at Edgbaston in 2023.

Ali claimed 27 wickets at an average of just 13 in his first campaign with Yorkshire, helping head coach Anthony McGrath's Tykes reach the quarter-final.

"My time at the club this year was brilliant," he said. "Whilst it was disappointing in how our T20 season finished, there's a lot to build on."

"Hassan's impact this year went beyond the pitch," said Yorkshire general manager of cricket Gavin Hamilton.

"Anthony and I have consistently said we want to build long term relationships with overseas players to provide that continuity that we value so highly. Hassan signing for a further two years is an illustration of that."

The fixtures are yet to be released for next year's Blast, but it is expected to start in May, with the final again at Edgbaston on Saturday 17 July.

articles.title: Ireland bounce back to beat UAE in Emerging Nations
articles.summary: Ireland Women recover from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in th...
articles.body:
Ireland Women 171-5 (20 overs): Lewis 71, Maritz 29; Thirukkumaran 2-20

United Arab Emirates Women 110-8 (20 overs): Oza 51, Dharnidharka 18; Murray 2-21

Ireland Women recovered from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in their second game in Ajman.

The UAE won the toss and elected to field first, with Lloyd Tennant's side producing a much stronger showing with the bat than they did against Sri Lanka.

The opening partnership of vice-captain Amy Hunter and captain Gaby Lewis laid the foundations for the Irish.

Hunter managed 29 runs from 27 balls before she was run out by Suraksha Kotte, while Lewis finished as Ireland's top run scorer with 71, including 12 fours and a six before she was dismissed by Indhuja Nandakumar in the 12th over.

Janani Thirukkumaran then forced out Louise Little (seven) in the next over and claimed her second wicket from Lara Maritz soon after, although she did add 29 to Ireland's tally from just 23 balls.

Laura Delany was 18 not out while Theertha Satish ran out Alana Dazell (11) as Ireland finished on 171-5 from their 20 overs.

The UAE had a nightmare start to their response as they lost Satish, Heena Hotchandhani and Rinitha Rajith all inside the first two overs.

Samaira Dharnidharka added 18 to the tally before becoming the fourth player to exit when she was bowled out by Cara Murray in the seventh over.

Esha Oza steadied the ship as she registered 51 runs from 45 balls with five fours and a six before being dismissed by Little.

The wickets continued to tumble as Thirukkumaran (13), Mehul Kulkarni (six) and Athige Sashikala Silva (four) all went as UAE fell well short of the target, ending with 110-8.

Ireland will next be in action on Monday when they face face Papua New Guinea (09:15 GMT) before rounding off their group campaign with a game against Scotland on Wednesday, 18 November (05:00 GMT).

articles.title: SEC Football Week 11 Predictions: Picks for Every Game
articles.summary: It's a dangerous week with Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and Kentucky all trying to avoid a third loss. Here are our previews and predictions for every SEC game...
articles.body:
There's no hard and fast rule that the College Football Playoff can't pick an at-large 9-3 team over a 10-2 team from a Power Four conference, but it's never happened before. You're on your own if you want to risk it. However, several SEC teams will be in CFP mix even with a third loss, but the freakout will come if Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and/or Kentucky get that third hit. Even worse, it's over if any of the three-loss teams – South Carolina, LSU, Ole Miss, or Missouri – lose. Here are our quick previews and predictions for every SEC game. – Predictions: ACC | Big Ten

Texas at LSU is the highest-profile SEC game of the week, but Missouri at Georgia could become a 2026 season-changer if the Tigers come up with something big.

It's a dangerous week for Alabama and Tennessee, going on the road to deal with desperate Mississippi State and Vanderbilt teams, respectively.

The pressure will mostly be on Kentucky. It dropped big in the CFP after loss to Tennessee, and it can't afford a loss to Florida.

Game Time: 12:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN2 Location: Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, MS The best thing to happen to Mississippi State during a five-game losing streak is the announced signing and return of star quarterback Kamario Taylor for next year. The Bulldog defense has been great, but the offense isn't moving well enough to push past a decent D. Auburn might be working too hard, but the defensive front is great at getting into the backfield and should come up with just enough big stops late to hold off a late Bulldog rally in a terrific game. Prediction: Auburn 27, Mississippi State 24 Consensus Line: Auburn -2.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 3

Game Time: 12:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: FirstBank Stadium, Nashville, TN No. 3 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, Alabama has love from the committee, and now it just has to finish the drill with Chattanooga and Auburn to close. First, it has to take down a Vanderbilt team that finally came up with its first SEC win of the season, beating Mississippi State 25-23. Alabama might not be its sharpest out of the gate – a hangover effect from the 31-13 win at LSU – but just when it seems like this might be interesting, the Commodore turnovers will come. Bama will convert off all three turnovers it generates. Prediction: Alabama 37, Vanderbilt 17 Consensus Line: Alabama -18.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 2.5

Game Time: 3:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kyle Field, College Station, TX Over the last few years, SEC fans have liked to use the word gauntlet when it comes to some teams' tough schedules. In Tennessee's case, the term applies, facing Alabama (CFP No. 3), South Carolina (CFP No. 17), and Kentucky (CFP No. 11) in the last three games, and with LSU up next after what qualifies as a week off at Texas A&M. The Aggies have been brutally close to finally pulling off something meaningful, but it's 1-5 in the SEC after a heartbreaking loss at South Carolina. The defense that can't generate a sack will have a hard time on third downs, but it'll be a tough effort at home that comes just short against a Volunteer defense that continues to take the ball away in bunches. Prediction: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 20 Consensus Line: Tennessee -2.5, o/u: 44.5 ATS Confidence: 2 | Must See: 3.5

Game Time: 3:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: Georgia -14.5, o/u: 47

Game Time: 4:15 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Memorial Stadium, Norman, OK There's nothing like seeing Georgia run out of the tunnel in your ballpark and watching it conduct a light scrimmage. Ole Miss didn't have any answers in a 42-7 loss to the CFP No. 1 team last week, and now it has to go on a roll to have any prayer of being considered for a high ranking by the playoff committee. Oklahoma continues its schizophrenic season, following every win with a loss. The defense was brilliant in a 23-7 win over Florida, but it won't have the same luck against an Ole Miss offense that needs to stop turning the ball over. Star Rebel running back Kewan Lacy is out for the season, but Trinidad Chambliss will bounce back from his rough day against the Bulldogs with a sharp day. Too many decent Oklahoma drives will end up with field goals. Prediction: Ole Miss 23, Oklahoma 19 Consensus Line: Oklahoma -1.5, o/u: 49.5 ATS Confidence: 2.5 | Must See: 3.5

Game Time: 6:15 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY CFP No. 11 Kentucky is still 7-2, with a playoff spot almost certainly for the taking if it can beat Missouri and Louisville. It has to get past the ugly 34-6 loss to Tennessee last week and keep its Florida groove going. The Wildcats have won four of the last five in the series. Before that, the Gators went 32-1 going back to 1986. It's all about the ground game with the Gators. They're 5-0 when running for over 120 yards, and 0-4 when running for that many or fewer. Kentucky got rumbled over by Tennessee, South Carolina, and Alabama. It's about to get hit by a good day from the Gators as they rebound big after last week. Prediction: Florida 28, Kentucky 24 Consensus Line: Kentucky -3.5, o/u: 52.5 ATS Confidence: 1.5 | Must See: 4

Game Time: 7:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: LSU -4.5, o/u: 46.5

Game Time: 7:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, AR Don't get totally caught up in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Soon, there will be big arguments about several three-loss teams and how worthy they might be. South Carolina started 2-3, but it's rolling with a four-game winning streak. That's not why the CFP No. 17 team has reason to dream of finishing in the top 12. Next week? Georgia. Beat the No. 1 team, drop Clemson, and all of a sudden, there will be a discussion. First, it has to get by a plucky Arkansas team that's far better than the 3-6 record might indicate. Nothing comes easy for the Gamecocks. Star quarterback LaNorris Sellers is banged up, but he's expected to go. Fortunately for 16, Arkansas doesn't have a pass rush to get to him. As long as Sellers is sniffing around a 65% completion rate, the Gamecocks will get through another grind of a game, and then it's on to the Bulldogs. Prediction: South Carolina 26, Arkansas 17 Consensus Line: South Carolina -7.5, o/u: 51.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 3

articles.title: 49ers’ Fred Warner Sparks Blunt Words From Cowboys’ Dak Prescott
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers defense will be looking to make life challenging for the Dallas Cowboys‘ offense. San Francisco’s defense will be looking to carry ov...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers defense will be looking to make life challenging for the Dallas Cowboys' offense. San Francisco's defense will be looking to carry over their defensive performance in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders into this game.

Against the Raiders, the Niners' defense recorded five takeaways, including three interceptions and two forced fumbles. Fred Warner was one of the players who recorded a takeaway against the Silver and Black.

Ahead of the game against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott shared his thoughts on facing Warner. Their offensive unit will have to account for where the linebacker is on the field and will need to hold on tight to the football, as Warner will be there to try to punch it out.

"He's probably the best linebacker in the NFL right now," Prescott told reporters on Nov. 12. "The way he plays the game mentally, reading the splits, reading the back, whether he's near or far, and making his different calls is impressive.

"Their defense is simple because he can get them into the right positions. They play fast, and they play hard. There's a little bit of a chess match there, but it's no different from play callers calling the plays. At the end of the day, it's about execution."

Warner has played 502 total snaps for the 49ers defense so far this season, leading to an 86.2 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran linebacker has recorded 54 solo tackles, generated five total pressures, one sack, 29 stops, and allowed an 84.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage.

49ers' Fred Warner Draws More Praise From Cowboys

Cowboys' DeMarvion Overshown won't be on the field at the same time as Warner, but the Dallas linebacker has a lot of respect for the 49ers star.

"I have the utmost respect for him," Overshown told reporters on Nov. 12 . "Since he came into this league, he's been a dog. He's been somebody you have to scout during the week. You have to know where 54 is and be aware when you're carrying the ball. He's the prototype linebacker. When you want to come into this league and be a great linebacker, you look at 54.

"You look at Fred and what he's done to change the game, especially how the linebacker position is played from sideline to sideline. I'd like to say he opened the doors for guys like me with my body type to come in and play four downs of football. I have the utmost respect for him. It's going to be good watching him play, but it's a battle at the end of the day. We want to come out as the linebacker unit that showed up and made the plays."

Fred Warner Gets Blunt on Facing Dallas' Offense

Meanwhile, Warner has plenty of respect for the Cowboys offense. On Nov. 11, the veteran linebacker spoke to the media and talked about Dallas' offense, as they'll be looking to make that unit's life difficult in this contest. Warner noted that the 49ers need to be on their A-game, given that the Cowboys can hurt them in the passing game.

"Dak [Prescott has] always played at a high level at the quarterback position," Warner told reporters . "A guy I got a ton of respect for as a player and as a leader for their team. He has some really elite weapons on the outside.

"CeeDee [Lamb] is having a tremendous year, getting a lot of targets, but also making use of those targets. George Pickens is also a huge weapon and has freakish ability when he gets the ball in his hands."

articles.title: Chicago Bears Win Despite Historic Mess Against Tampa Bay
articles.summary: The Bears became the first NFL team to win with five turnovers and nine penalties. Coach Ben Johnson says the manner of play must improve before the season e...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears made history on Sunday night by winning a game despite committing five turnovers, taking nine penalties, and failing to rush for a single 10‑yard gain. Yahoo Sports noted this odd mix of errors and victory makes the team look different than any other squad in the league this season. No other team in NFL history has ever blown a 14-point lead at home, taken so many penalties, and still secured a win against a team like Tampa Bay.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson admitted the team did not play their best football during the 27-24 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 8. He told reporters that while the win is what matters most right now, the style of play leaves room for growth. "At the end of the day, that's the end goal that we're looking for," Johnson said, referring to the victory itself. He also noted that the players in the locker room knew they had underperformed even though they got the win.

Johnson felt a specific energy from the group despite the sloppy stats, which he called a positive sign for the future. "I felt that from our crew, which is a good thing," Johnson said. The team now sits at 7-2 as they head into their bye week, giving them time to fix the issues that plagued them against Tampa Bay. The coach said good teams can win without playing their A‑game.

Key players like linebacker Devin Bush and edge rusher Austin Booker stepped up when the offense struggled to move the ball. Johnson commended Bush for delivering a top-tier performance as a Chicago Bear, a sight that was remarkable. He further emphasized Booker's intensity and effort, observing that the defensive players continue improving week in and week out. These individual efforts helped the team overcome the five turnovers and the loss of a 14-point lead.

The bye week offers a crucial chance for the roster to heal up before the final stretch of the season. Several key players, including running back Kyle Monangai and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, have missed games this year and need this time to recover. Quarterback Caleb Williams also gets a week to rest his hamstring, while wide receiver Luther Burden III uses the time to recover from a concussion suffered in the game.

Yahoo Sports reported that the power rankings have shifted dramatically at the midway point of the season, with only half of the preseason top 10 teams remaining in the top 10. The Bears have moved into a strong position, but the coach says the team still needs to improve its play to reach its full potential. Johnson said the team needs to continue evolving so they can win in the right manner, not just by luck or grit alone. The team will use this week to review the first nine games and decide what areas need the most work before the season ends.

articles.title: Texans special teams coach is pumped to play in ‘heavenly’ Cleveland weather
articles.summary: Unlike most players and coaches in the NFL, Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frank Ross relishes playing in inclement weather, as it adds another lay...
articles.body:
Unlike most players and coaches in the NFL, Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frank Ross relishes playing in inclement weather, as it adds another layer of gamesmanship.

The Texans will visit the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, and while some are worried about the windy forecast, Ross is not bothered at all, even though the Browns are still undefeated at home.

When a reporter asked him about dealing with the "bad weather" in Cleveland, Ross had a quick counter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I call it good weather! That's your opinion. I call it good weather! I think we are going to heaven," said Ross in the video posted by The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov.

"No matter when we go out there, we gotta have to test it. We gonna make sure we make those micro-adjustments relative to which end you're kicking. Cleveland's got two different ends. You have to know which way you're going. To be able to make those and trust your line," said Ross.

He also expressed excitement for snapper Austin Brinkman, who could play a major role for Houston, as windy weather would deeply affect the offensive strategy of both squads.

"Experience. That's the only way you can improve in that. You gotta go in and do that," added Ross.

"We've got two snappers going against each other. They both played at the University of West Virginia. We're gonna go handle the elements. We know they (Browns) can as well."

The Texans are coming off a win against the Los Angeles Chargers, 44-22, while the Browns are looking to snap a two-game skid.

articles.title: The Outlook - Week 10 (SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL)
articles.summary: The Outlook is The Huddle's new matchups column. Kevin Tompkins will break down every fantasy-relevant player from each team every week.
articles.body:
Hey, folks! We're back with our third and final block of games for the Week 10 NFL slate, and we're covering all three late games, Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football!

We've compiled the game groupings here to make it easier to find the games you want:

Block 1: WAS-NYG, NE-DET, KC-ATL, HOU-CLE, MIA-IND

Block 2: JAC-TEN, MIN-GB, CAR-NO, BUF-NYJ

Block 3: SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL

"The Outlook" will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues!

I'm incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I'll do my best to answer them for you.

All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Thursday for SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN and LAC-BAL.

Teams on bye in Week 9: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Implied Point Total: Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 17

Must-Start Players: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba

In Week 8, both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to action against the Chicago Bears in a gross, ugly backfield split that didn't benefit either back. In Week 9 against a softer opponent in the Cardinals, the Seahawks were able to get the running game going a little bit in neutral and positive game scripts. Both players were heavily involved, but Charbonnet saw more work than Price. Charbonnet (17) out-touched Price (13), and George Holani was essentially phased out of regular work with just two snaps. Charbonnet was the lead back on the game's first two drives, after which Price and Charbonnet alternated drives for the rest of the game. Price actually led the Seahawks with 54 receiving yards in a very muted game started by Drew Lock .

In this configuration, Charbonnet is ahead of Price for now, and in most situations, Charbonnet should get the edge in receiving work. Think of it as the early Kyren Williams/Blake Corum split, but with Corum getting a bit more of the receiving work while Williams plays the majority of the snaps. Charbonnet certainly isn't Williams, but if Seattle can find some offensive rhythm, both backs can achieve fantasy viability.

Fantasy Advice: With the Raiders giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to backfields, this is a great spot for the Seahawks backs. I'd be happy to fire up Charbonnet as a low-end RB2 and Price as a low-end flex play who should get enough work to matter here.

With Kirk Cousins now back in Pizza Ranch country , Mendoza will make his first NFL start after watching Cousins for nine games and getting some garbage-time throws in Week 5's blowout loss in New England. Mendoza will immediately be thrown into the fire at home against the Seahawks before having to travel to Denver to play the Broncos. More than likely, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and head coach and playcaller Klint Kubiak will do their best not to put too much on Mendoza's plate early on. That means conservative playcalling and getting the ball out quickly. It may also mean more running plays, so we'll see how the Raiders navigate these waters over the next few weeks.

Fantasy Advice: Mendoza is worth picking up as a speculative stash. Trusting him as a fantasy starter against Seattle? I doubt anybody is that desperate, unless you are exactly that: desperate.

The split among these Vegas running backs persists, and Mike Washington Jr. took a bit of a backseat to Ashton Jeanty in terms of touches and overall playing time. Jeanty handled an overwhelming 63% of the snaps and 73% of the routes, earning seven targets and catching five passes for -5 yards. I'm sure the anti-PPR bros were up in arms about Jeanty earning seven points on that receiving work and his 25 rushing yards. Meanwhile, Washington's -0.5 yards per carry likely isn't impressing anybody. Jeanty has a bit of R.J. Harvey in him right now with his role, and Washington is somebody you don't need to be plugging into your fantasy lineups. Luckily, Jeanty's receiving floor could pay some dividends for a young quarterback making his first NFL start.

Fantasy Advice: I'd be fine with Jeanty as a flex against the Seahawks in Week 10, but his fantasy stock has really fallen over the last month with Kubiak's meddling. To be fair, Jeanty hasn't exactly helped himself here, despite reportedly being banged up.

Implied Point Total: Rams 24.5, Cardinals 15

It's been the running game that has carried Stafford's offense over the past month. Stafford's best fantasy finish was QB11 against the Raiders in Week 7. Since then, he's finished as QB22 against the Chargers and QB20 against the Commanders. He hasn't had Davante Adams in any of those three games. Now, at least for the foreseeable future, he won't have Puka Nacua either.

You could still make the case for starting Stafford with Nacua in the lineup. Without him, however, it's a collection of young, inexperienced players, his running backs and a glut of tight ends. That doesn't make for a very enticing fantasy quarterback, especially when the Rams' running backs have been driving the offense and they have a below-average matchup against fantasy running backs on tap. I'd be looking elsewhere, despite the Cardinals being one of the best matchups for any quarterback.

Fantasy Advice: Stafford is a solid QB2 option who should be able to provide a usable floor, but a ceiling game is almost impossible to expect given the injuries to both Adams and Nacua.

This Rams offense will have to rely almost entirely on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for now, with Adams and Nacua out of the wide receiver lineup. Luckily, Corum has been on a massive heater with five consecutive top-20 fantasy finishes and at least 58 yards and a touchdown in each of those games. Meanwhile, Williams should be able to pick up some of the target-earning slack without Nacua while continuing to provide solid production on the ground. Williams had his worst fantasy performance of the season, finishing as RB25 last week with three receptions and 61 yards from scrimmage against the Commanders. However, if there's a time for anybody to pick up the pieces of the offense after these two major injuries, it's now for both Williams and Corum.

Fantasy Advice: Both Williams and Corum are viable fantasy RB2s against the Cardinals, with Williams getting a slight edge in PPR formats and the two being nearly even in value in half-PPR.

It feels like Allgeier's 36.1 fantasy-point outburst against the Cowboys was quite the outlier, as he went right back to averaging 2.7 yards per carry against the Seahawks. To be fair, that was expected. The outburst came against the Cowboys, and he returned to being a plodder against the Seahawks in Seattle. Even more factors are working against him now. Allgeier faces another tough defense at home in Week 10 against the Rams, and Bam Knight may return to work in tandem with him. With Gardner Minshew injured and placed on IR, rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback this weekend. That combination of factors really pushes Allgeier down the rankings and makes him a volume-based back who may not even get enough opportunities if Knight returns and takes some carries away from him!

Fantasy Advice: Allgeier is a very shaky flex play in Week 10, and I'd be looking elsewhere for another flex starter. I'd only play him if I have even shakier options at flex.

Implied Point Total: 49ers 29.5, Cowboys 26

Must-Start Players: QB Brock Purdy, RB Christian McCaffrey, TE George Kittle

The 49ers will welcome back Samuel with open arms for the first time since Week 5 when they head to AT&T Stadium to play the Cowboys in what should be a shootout featuring the highest game total of Week 10 (55.5 points). Samuel returns at a critical time, as the team also acquired Keenan Allen from the Colts at the trade deadline to help bolster a wide receiver position ravaged by injuries. The 49ers have already used an NFL-high 10 players at the position this season, with Allen becoming the 11th once he takes his first snap as a 49er. Samuel should operate as the main passing-game target after missing three games and four weeks, including the bye, so it's wheels up for Deebo this week.

Fantasy Advice: Samuel has practiced in a limited capacity, but he is on track to play in Week 10. Fire him up as a WR3 option this week, as he should be a key target for Brock Purdy against Dallas.

After a shaky first six games of the season against some tough defenses, Prescott has entered a nice stretch with easier matchups. He's been a top-10 fantasy quarterback over the last three weeks against the Eagles, Cardinals and Colts. Now the 49ers come to AT&T Stadium, and with a 55.5-point game total, this matchup should feature plenty of offense. Sign me up for Prescott, who could get 40-plus pass attempts in a neutral game script if the Cowboys keep things close with San Francisco. If they fall behind, we could see plenty of trailing-game-script passing volume. Either way, we'll love to see it.

Fantasy Advice: Prescott is one of the best quarterback starts of the week for fantasy managers. Normally, I hate hearing it on my TV, but I'll join in with a signature Dak " Yeahhhh, here we goooo! "

Among running backs outside the Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs top tier, there perhaps is no more bankable volume play than Williams this season. Williams is currently the RB5. Despite averaging just 4.1 yards per carry, he has 10 total touchdowns and is averaging 70 yards per game. While the 55.5-point game total should give us some offensive fireworks, the 49ers have allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing backfields this season. The sledding might be tougher than usual for Williams, but he should get a handful of opportunities near the end zone if this game produces as many points as oddsmakers expect. Williams' volume should be nearly guaranteed, as backup Tyler Goodson sprained his ACL and MCL. The Cowboys may therefore bring up recent signee Kendre Miller and/or Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to back up Williams.

Fantasy Advice: He might be a pure volume play this week against the 49ers, but Williams has been solid this season. Consider him a locked-in RB2 who should get some green-zone touches in a high-scoring game environment.

George Pickens sat out Week 9 against Indianapolis with a hamstring injury, and he's put together two limited practices this week as of this writing. That continues a string of three practices last week, despite his sitting out against the Colts after playing through the injury against the Cardinals and earning just three targets, with two receptions for 48 yards. If Pickens can't go, you're giving a sizable bump to Ryan Flournoy , who had 100% route participation without Pickens in Week 9 but managed just two catches for 53 yards. However, in a fruitful game environment where there should be plenty of scoring, the potential for much more is always there. The Cowboys will also be without Jake Ferguson , so the offense may become more concentrated around the wide receivers, who will have to do the heavy lifting in terms of targets and opportunity.

Fantasy Advice: Pickens is a locked-in WR2 if he suits up for the Cowboys in Week 10. Without Pickens, Flournoy would be a solid mid-range WR3. Even if Pickens plays, Flournoy should get enough routes to be a viable flex option with plenty of scoring potential in this game against San Francisco.

Implied Point Total: Bengals 26.5, Steelers 23

The Steelers were on bye in Week 9, so hopefully Aaron Rodgers was able to reset, listen to some Bon Iver and get back to the Rodgers we saw from Weeks 3 through 5. During that stretch, he put up three straight QB12-or-better fantasy finishes. That also coincided with the Steelers throwing much deeper downfield, which Pittsburgh may have to do to keep up with Cincinnati's incredible passing game. We know Rodgers loves to check the ball down, but after recording 300-plus air yards in three of the first four weeks, the Steelers have totaled fewer than 200 air yards as a team over their last four games. Condensing the field allows defenders to get to your checkdowns and running game much quicker, so hopefully some field-stretching is on the menu in Week 10.

Fantasy Advice: If Rodgers can keep up with the Bengals' offense, or at least make a concerted effort to do so in Week 10, it will be a good week for fantasy managers. He's a solid fantasy QB2 who is streamable in this matchup.

In Week 8, Warren had 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, but he got banged up after a fumble and the ensuing pileup for the ball. Dowdle ended up taking most of the fourth-quarter carries and finished with a solid 15-56 rushing line, along with a first-quarter score on the team's second drive. With the Week 9 bye, Warren should be ready to lead the backfield, but Dowdle gets more than enough work to make him a viable flex play against the Bengals. Dowdle has also surprised in the receiving department, thanks to Rodgers checking the ball down. He's on pace for more than 50 targets and 44 receptions on top of his rushing work. That's a solid floor, and you could do worse in your flex.

Fantasy Advice: Dowdle is one of the better contingent plays in fantasy, but he definitely has enough standalone value to warrant flex consideration in Week 10.

While the Steelers' wide receivers have been much more "miss" than "hit" this season, this week's matchup against Cincinnati gives both DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard a good shot at getting back into fantasy managers' good graces. The targets have been there for Metcalf, but he's barely caught half of them and is on pace for just 803 yards this season. Meanwhile, Bernard's short-area target-earning and YAC ability fit Rodgers' dump-off style, but the rookie has been inconsistent after a rash of injuries hit the Steelers' wide receiver room. It's not a matter of getting the ball to the best players in the offense; it's simply a matter of whoever is open. That lack of target concentration in this passing game has pushed down the value of both options for fantasy. The hope is that with a matchup against the Bengals, a high game total and the Steelers playing as road underdogs, Pittsburgh will have to throw the ball with some volume for a change.

Fantasy Advice: Given Metcalf's disappointing first half and Bernard's inconsistency, both are solid flex options rather than full-blown starters in what appears to be a good game environment.

Must-Start Players: QB Joe Burrow, WR Ja'Marr Chase, WR Tee Higgins

Even with Samaje Perine getting more carries than Brown in Week 9, that was more a product of the game script, with the Bengals leading by more than two scores in the third quarter and holding a two-touchdown lead well into the fourth. Positive game scripts aren't going to benefit Brown in most cases, but neutral and negative game scripts will unlock more carries and especially more work in the receiving game. I'm not as worried as some in the industry who are sounding the alarm about Brown, especially with the possibility of a game in which the Steelers grind things to a halt with their pace. To be fair, the Bengals are a slow-paced team, too, and Pittsburgh should be able to keep the game close. The Steelers also allow the second-most running back receptions per game this season, which benefits Brown greatly.

Fantasy Advice: I still like Brown as a mid-range RB2 with plenty of PPR upside in what should be a close game in Week 10.

Implied Point Total: Ravens 21.5, Chargers 17

While McConkey is technically the WR1 for the Chargers, I don't know how you can trust him. McConkey was ruled out shortly after their Week 9 game started because of back issues that surfaced during pregame warmups. Why wasn't that news communicated before the game? Anyway, those who started him (myself included on a couple of teams) got a big fat zero, and people will remember that in perpetuity. People STILL talk about the Tee Higgins, DeAndre Hopkins and Julio Jones decoy games years later! It's hard to put McConkey, with his litany of injuries and the team's 0-8 record, in any circle of trust right now for fantasy purposes.

Fantasy Advice: McConkey is a very deep flex play and should only be started in the most dire of circumstances against Baltimore.

In terms of real-life NFL quarterbacking, Brissett is definitely on one of the bottom rungs. For this Ravens team, which has gone through quite a bit with rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano seeing what was essentially two games' worth of action, acquiring Brissett is a godsend. Brissett won't light the world on fire, but steadiness and competence are the goals here. With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and riding a four-game losing streak, this is a season-saving measure. Obviously, this kind of move is music to the ears of fantasy managers who have Zay Flowers , so feeding him and the secondary weapons around him is paramount to getting back into the postseason hunt. All of that affects what we do here in fantasy, so we'll see how much of a leash offensive coordinator Declan Doyle gives Brissett in his first start as a Raven against the 0-8 Chargers.

Fantasy Advice: Well, it's a good matchup for Brissett, and with plenty of quarterback turnover this week, plus Caleb Williams on bye, you could do worse than starting Brissett in Week 10.

With an undrafted free-agent rookie quarterback in Fagnano under center in Week 9, you could say it was a little difficult to move the ball against the Jaguars last Thursday. That's certainly understandable, which is why the best chance to move the ball was through the running game and Henry. He did well given the circumstances, finishing with 57 rushing yards. He was outproduced by Justice Hill overall, but that was thanks to a long 65-yard touchdown run toward the end of the game when the Jaguars were already in cruise control defensively.

You can expect a little more respect for the passing game in the weeks ahead and certainly this week as Brissett takes over for Fagnano. Baltimore brought in Brissett because of the injuries and ineffectiveness of its other quarterbacks, and he should at least be able to move the ball through the air. Anything helps when it comes to pushing defenders out of the box and creating more running lanes for Henry. More importantly, Brissett should help the Ravens stay out of negative game scripts, which can erase Henry from games.

Fantasy Advice: Henry is in the high-end RB2 tier this week against the Chargers, a favorable opponent for getting back on track.

articles.title: Henry and Young shine as New Zealand thrash India by 244 runs
articles.summary: New Zealand trail India 2-1 and can no longer win the five-match series, but they can level it in Sunday’s final game.
articles.body:
Matt Henry took six wickets and Will Young struck a century as New Zealand thrashed a ragged India by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Mount Maunganui on Friday.

Henry removed Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer, all without scoring, in the first over of India’s chase to tear the top order apart. The visitors needed a massive 334 for victory.

New Zealand made 333 all out in the last over after being asked to bat, with Young punishing two simple drops by Indian fielders to bring up his fifth ODI hundred.

India never stood a chance of chasing the total after Henry’s heavenly opening over.

Rohit edged his first ball to slip, Kohli was bowled facing his fourth ball, and then Iyer was pegged on his back leg to fall lbw.

India’s rebuild never happened, with Ishan Kishan top-scoring with just 27 as India were rolled for 89.

Henry ended with 6-27 and Matthew Fisher took 3-31.

New Zealand’s imposing total came off the back of Young’s 125 from 108 balls, including 14 fours and four sixes.

Young and Tim Seifert combined for an 85-run opening partnership.

While Young rode his early luck – dropped twice in two balls when on five in the second over, first by slip Rohit and then by wicketkeeper Kishan – Seifert played the aggressor with a brisk 39-ball 50.

When Seifert fell for 58, Nick Kelly and Dean Foxcroft soon followed, playing reckless shots.

Young found better support in Finn Allen, the pair putting on 90 runs in just 65 balls as they seized on wayward Indian bowling.

Young’s first 50 came from 49 balls, and his second from just 39 balls as he hit regular boundaries through the middle overs.

Allen made 41 from 30 deliveries, including five fours and two sixes.

Axar Patel took 2-39 from 10 overs as India pulled the innings back late, while Auqib Nabi had 2-59 and Gurnoor Brar 2-69.

New Zealand trail India 2-1 and can no longer win the five-match series, but they can avoid defeat if they ⁠win the final match at the same venue on Sunday. The third match was abandoned due to rain.

articles.title: Manchester United hires Mauricio Pochettino as its new head coach, US set to begin search for replacement
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been confirmed as the next head coach of Manchester United, the team announced on social media on Friday.
articles.body: Mauricio Pochettino has been confirmed as the next head coach of Manchester United, the team announced on social media on Friday. The experienced head coach takes over from Michael Carrick, who was fired by the club on Thursday. Pochettino will continue in his current position as US Men’s National Team (USMNT) head coach for this international break before crossing over the Atlantic to take charge of the Red Devils. “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players,” Manchester United said in its statement. The job awaiting Pochettino at Old Trafford is gigantic. First, he has to work out how to fit into the club’s complicated hierarchy. The Argentine will then need to work on a playing roster that looks short of quality and motivate players who look mentally fragile. Perhaps most importantly, the new boss will need to keep the fans on side. Even when things got ugly under Carrick, the supporters chose to back the former midfielder, putting the blame firmly at the feet of the players and the club’s hierarchy. The consensus with fans and the British media is that the current culture around the club is so toxic that it’s almost impossible for any head coach to succeed. Pochettino will face a tough task trying to prove that wrong. A fond farewell Sentiments among supporters of the “Stars and Stripes” regarding the Argentine’s departure might be mixed, but USMNT top brass were grateful to Pochettino for his stint. “Mauricio has left a lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture,” US Soccer CEO JT Batson said in a statement. “What we are most proud of goes beyond the wins. He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the Youth National Teams to the senior team.” An emotional Pochettino addressed the media during a press conference held on Friday ahead of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal first leg against Haiti. “Normally it’s the opposite, you’re sacked and you cry because you want to stay and you are sacked,” the tearful Pochettino said. “It’s never an ideal situation when this type of thing happens but like in life, football goes quick.” The head coach spoke of the “amazing memories” he had as head coach and reiterated his commitment to the USMNT across this international break. Pochettino took over as head coach of the US in 2024 and was tasked with leading the team into a home World Cup. While the US impressed in the group stage and cruised past Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32, the team eventually crashed out to Belgium in disappointing circumstances. The Americans were outplayed from start to finish in the Round of 16 matchup before succumbing to a 4-1 defeat against better opposition. “The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country,” Pochettino said in Friday’s statement. Who will replace Poch with the US? If there’s one thing about this current US setup, it’s certainly ambitious. Pochettino represented a real coup for the program after managing at the highest level with Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. But according to reports, the next head coach might just be an even more impressive get. According to reporters with The Athletic, legendary manager Pep Guardiola is a top target to replace the outgoing Pochettino and would certainly be a headline-grabbing appointment. Guardiola has won all there is to win in club soccer, and after almost two decades working with the very best, could the former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City head coach set his sights on the international game? It wouldn’t be the first time the US has shown an interest in Guardiola and they may feel now is the best chance they’ll get to attract the iconic head coach. “Our supporters, our sponsors, our donors, our fans are very supportive around making sure that we have the resources to achieve our goals including having a world class coach and we’re appreciative of that support and look forward to that being a key part of our way of winning going forward,” US Soccer CEO Batson said in the press conference on Friday. While Guardiola might be the top prize, the US may also look a bit closer to home in its efforts to succeed Pochettino. BJ Callaghan is certainly one name that fits the bill. The 45-year-old has impressed in his job with Nashville SC and has led the team to a league-best 77 points in the MLS as it topped the Eastern Conference in the regular season. The head coach is also no stranger to the US national setup. Callaghan was an interim head coach for the team in 2023 and even managed to lead the side to victory in the CONCACAF Nations League during his brief time in charge. Another name familiar to US fans is Steve Cherundolo. Cherundolo had a successful playing career in Germany and was a stalwart for the US national side across his 87 appearances. As he’s currently charge of the under-23 national side, Cherundolo would also be familiar with the setup and requirements needed should he advance to the top job. This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.title: Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup 2026: Sharks, ladders and a four-year plan - how England won
articles.summary: England's triumph at the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup was built on an aggressive approach by head coach Tom Coyd - which included encouraging his players to see themselves like sharks.
articles.body:
Sharks and ladders played their part in England's Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup success.

As they chased success in Australia, they had a ladder in team meetings to help them visualise their route to the trophy - spray painting a rung gold with each victory.

And they spent time comparing themselves to lifeguards and sharks.

It was all part of coach Tom Coyd's masterplan, which boiled down to one thing - taking an aggressive approach.

It worked. On Friday, they beat France 50-38 in the World Cup final in Wollongong, to defend the trophy they won in Manchester four years ago.

Not that Coyd ever used the word 'defend'. He has steered clear of that term since England lifted the trophy in November 2022. For four years, he has wanted his team to have a more attacking mindset in the pursuit of back-to-back world titles.

His team were positive from the off at this tournament, amassing 386 points across the group stage and semi-finals while conceding just 68.

And his approach ultimately ensured that England became the first nation to win the Wheelchair World Cup three times.

"I think your reality is the story that you tell yourself," Coyd said. "And the narrative that we felt might be upon us coming in was that we are here to defend and we are here to retain.

"We found that framing to be defensive, to be a bit passive - and knowing that we've been world number one since November 2022, we wanted to come in with an attacking mindset and with a hunter's mindset.

"If we had not spent the last four years talking about defending the World Cup, we weren't going to spend the last three weeks [at this tournament] talking about it either.

"We wanted to prime the group to be forward thinking, to attack the attack when we didn't have the ball - and when we did have the ball, to be a shark smelling blood in the water."

Across the World Cup finals of 2013, 2017 and 2022, the game's two powerhouse nations had been separated by a total of only 10 points - two in the first match, and four in the following two.

However, on the western coast of Australia - around 70 miles south of where England won the inaugural competition in Sydney back in 2008 - Coyd's group of players served up an exceptional display.

Having initially forged ahead, England then fought back from a 22-10 deficit before powering to victory against Cyril Torres' uncompromising French side.

"I think the way they executed tonight was just outstanding," Coyd added.

"I don't think France have moved backwards. If anything, they looked hungrier than I've ever seen them.

"But the rate of which these 10 lads have moved on just blew my mind. I'm so proud of them."

England win Wheelchair World Cup for third time

The brothers and their dad driving England's World Cup bid

'Talisman' King & England's assured leaders

Thirty minutes into the final, England were in danger of disappointment. France, having trailed 10-0, had responded with 22 unanswered points to take control.

However, that dominance was fleeting. By the break, tries from Rob Hawkins - recently crowned the world's best player for a third time - and Jack Brown had restored order.

And when captain Lewis King led a short half-time huddle, it delivered a moment of reassurance for the group that quietly helped lay the platform for success.

"Lewis' presence is everything for this team," added Coyd.

"He always finds the right words at the right time. That's before, during and after games.

"Even in those moments during the match today, where we've been calling it a riptide - continuing on a surfing theme, when it feels like the waves are going against you, even though you feel like you don't deserve that.

"The steadiness and the composure that Lewis just lives and breathes so innately - the boys feed off of it. He's without the doubt the talisman for this group."

Joe Coyd - the head coach's younger brother, who scored four of England's nine tries - added: "We don't need a massive rousing 'let's all go together' type of speech.

"We've got such confidence in each other and we've all seen the work we're doing and we challenge each other in such a good, positive way.

"Tom's not even [been] in the changing room in the last messages today and hasn't been all tournament."

Jack Brown, playing at his fifth World Cup and earning his third winner's medal, added: "I don't think the team missed that [not having a rousing speech] because we saw it as a confidence in the team.

"We knew what we had to do and we knew that we had so many leaders in our team."

articles.title: How doing psychedelic drugs with Mike Tyson helped documentarian understand the baddest man on the planet
articles.summary: Why did Mike Tyson fight Jake Paul? Floyd Russ says that it was the most innocent question that garnered the most unexpected response.
articles.body: Why did Mike Tyson fight Jake Paul? Floyd Russ says that it was the most innocent question that garnered the most unexpected response. He had asked the former world heavyweight boxing champion why he climbed back into the ring at the age of 58. “And he goes, ‘The toad told me to. Anytime I have a big decision to make, I consult the toad.’” The American-born documentary filmmaker knew that his Netflix project to chronicle one of the most compelling, complicated and arguably most misunderstood athletes of the 20th century would be an adventure, but he surely couldn’t have imagined that he’d end up going on a psychedelic trip with the fighter once dubbed “The Baddest Man On The Planet.” “You’re dealing with a very emotional person, his life is a complete roller coaster,” he told CNN Sports. “You might get one Mike Tyson one day and another Mike Tyson the other day. You might even get a different Mike Tyson after lunch. That’s something that we kind of prepared for, but it’s also something you can’t really prepare for.” The four-hour “Tyson,” which dropped on Netflix last month, profiles Tyson’s rise, fall and the subsequent rehabilitation of his reputation and brand. The film chronicles the extreme poverty and even depravity of his upbringing in New York, his hedonistic lifestyle and ill-fated first marriage, the allegations of domestic abuse, the biting of opponents Evander Holyfield and Lennox Lewis, the rape conviction for which he still maintains his innocence, and the personal bereavements that have haunted much of his life. In his role as the interviewer, Russ at times seems to play the role of Tyson’s therapist, leading him back inside some of his darkest memories without getting sucked in himself. “If he’s crying, I’m trying to keep it together,” he said, “trying to move the conversation forward, making sure that we don’t unravel.” When Tyson was on the brink of becoming the youngest ever world heavyweight champion, he lost both his mother and his mentor and trainer Cus D’Amato, and his emotions are rarely far from the surface. “I love the line that he has in the first episode, he’s crying, he’s like, ‘What’s wrong with me? Is there something wrong with me?’” Russ recalled. “‘All these motherf**kers are going to think that I’m weak,’ when it’s quite the opposite. To show your emotions is a strength.” Tyson’s physical strength has been well documented. The laser-focused savagery with which he demolished so many opponents made him irresistible to the fans and the media in the 1980s and ‘90s. But Russ, who went toe to toe with Tyson over eight intense interview sessions spanning close to a year, says that it was Tyson’s vulnerability that was so compelling. “Behind that masculine figure, there’s a fragile man. He’s utterly fragile, and I think that’s something that I find the most refreshing about him,” he said. The Toad Russ says that couldn’t think of a more “epic subject” to tackle as a filmmaker, and he quickly learned that his best strategy in each round of the interrogation was to emulate Tyson’s famous fighting style: Get onto the front foot and take it to the opponent. “With Mike, it’s about respect,” he said. “If you can challenge him, he will respect you. He’s media trained in his own way, meaning he has no media training, and he will either like what you were talking about and respect you and go to an interesting place, or just shut down. If you just ask him all the questions he wants to be asked, he’s not going to respect you.” But if Tyson was going to drop his defenses and let him all the way in, Russ came to realize that he would have to do something more. “He was, like, ‘If you do the toad with me, I’m going to answer all your questions.’ That was basically what it came down to, and I was put in a very interesting position,” he said. “Toad” is shorthand for the psychoactive compound 5-MeO-DMT, a Schedule I controlled substance, which is derived from the venom of the Sonoran Desert Toad. Tyson’s wife, Lahika “Kiki” Spicer, describes it as “ego death” and Tyson believes it has helped him face his many demons, kick a cocaine habit and be more present for his family. According to Russ, Tyson has sought out the treatment “hundreds of times.” “At first, I thought it was a joke,” he explained. “He’s like, ‘If it wasn’t for the toad, you wouldn’t be interviewing me. None of it, nobody would even be talking about Mike Tyson. I would probably be dead.’” In the final episode of “Tyson,” the boxer asks Russ to do toad with him. “I don’t know if I can,” the director is heard responding nervously. Russ says that Tyson mentioned it often throughout the project, and when Spicer called to say, “Mike would like to do the toad with you next week,” he knew that he had a decision to make. Ultimately, Russ agreed, knowing that it would also seal the bond between them. Russ says that Tyson never talks about what specifically he experiences while under the influence of the drug, but he documented him inhaling the smoke via a pipe, lying back in a peaceful outdoor setting, grunting, sometimes laughing and sometimes shouting as if in a state of anguish. When it was Russ’s turn, he said that he felt faint for 20 to 30 minutes, he felt as though he was transported to a different place, and then he calmly woke up. “It feels like you’re reborn, basically. The way I describe it is if you could remember your own birth,” he said. There to greet him as he came around was the tattooed face of one of the once-most feared athletes in the world. “There’s Mike Tyson, like two feet to the right of me, looking back at me and he’s just like, ‘How are you doing?’ And I just started laughing,” Russ said. The scene is a metaphor for Tyson’s own rebirth. A man who came from nothing, who had everything and then lost it all, who has spent his life trying to find himself, seems to finally be at some kind of peace. But that doesn’t mean he’s able to watch the film of his life without experiencing some discomfort. Russ says that he hasn’t spoken with Tyson since the film aired, but he’s heard from Spicer. “It was not a matter of him liking it,” Russ told CNN Sports of that conversation. “It was a matter of him being able to stand it. The first episode made him cry, she told me. If he liked it too much, then I would feel like I didn’t do my job.”

articles.title: Al Michaels chokes up during moving tribute to Dan Hicks on Thursday Night Football – his best moment in years
articles.summary: Al Michaels choked up during his Thursday Night Football tribute to Dan Hicks, whose death left behind wife Hannah Storm and three daughters.
articles.body: Sometimes, home run hitters blast the baseball out of the park even when they're past their prime, and Al Michaels did exactly that on the Thursday Night Football telecast on Prime. Michaels, calling the Washington Commanders victory over the New York Giants, was his usual adept and seasoned self, delivering the play-by-play of the game that actually kept our attention because it was entertaining. Then in the fourth quarter, he delivered a eulogy on behalf of Prime for NBC broadcaster Dan Hicks, who died unexpectedly Thursday of an undetermined acute illness. NBC'S MIKE TIRICO SIDELINED BY HEALTH ISSUE AHEAD OF BEARS VS. BUCCANEERS ON SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL And it was Michaels at his finest. "The sports broadcasting business was shocked to learn this morning of the passing of Dan Hicks," Michaels began. "Dan joined NBC Sports in 1992, provided captions to so many iconic moments in golf, tennis, and Notre Dame football. "And he and Rowdy Gaines turned the calling of swimming in multiple Olympics into an art form. He was genial, he was compassionate, great company, had a world-class sense of humor. "On this very rough day for so many of us we send ..." That is the point where Michaels began to choke up on air. It wasn't him bursting out in tears. It was him pausing for a beat, his voice cracking just slightly, as his compassion and sympathy for what he was about to say next obviously was on his mind. The last part, where Michaels realized the tragedy of the death leaves behind a family broken by the loss was moving. And sad. It was Michaels at his best in years. The fact Michaels somehow recovered and finished the tribute was professionalism at its height. The audience felt his pain and the pain of the family left behind and saw the recovery in real time. It was humanity and emotion pouring from Michaels and anyone who watched felt it. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Moments later, Michaels continued his football play-by-play duties. He was again composed and in the moment. And this: Michaels celebrated his 82nd birthday on Thursday. It is possible, perhaps even likely, that as he was delivering those sad words about Dan Hicks and his family, Al Michaels had a moment where he realized his own mortality.
