articles.title: 6 NHL Teams That Need to Rebuild and Trade Vets ASAP
articles.summary: We're more than one month into the 2026-27 NHL season, and while we still don't have the clearest picture of the playoff bubble, we're sure getting a sense of the bottom of the barrel of the league.
articles.body:
We're more than one month into the 2026-27 NHL season, and while we still don't have the clearest picture of the playoff bubble, we're sure getting a sense of the bottom of the barrel of the league.

We're also getting a sense of which teams need to start thinking about assets they can and should trade at the deadline to start rebuilds that clearly need to begin at this point.

Here are six NHL teams that need to trade their veterans and blow it all up.

The Blackhawks are having an absolutely dreadful season, to say the least. They have a 5-13-1 record; they sit nine points behind the next-best team in the Central, and they have a league-worst -36 goal differential.

Even if they weren't expected to make the playoffs this season, they've got a whole lot of work to do if they're to take the next step in their rebuild. Their main priorities need to be finally finding Connor Bedard that elusive, long-term winger and strengthening the overall defense. Trading a player like Teuvo Teravainen at the deadline could at least open up some roster space and cap space as the Blackhawks search for that winger.

Columbus has fallen behind even Philadelphia in the basement of the Metropolitan Division standings, and it's just getting worse amidst this three-game losing streak. They're 7-10-0 with a -12 goal differential, and you're starting to wonder if GM Don Waddell has started making calls.

While Zach Werenski vetoed a trade that would've sent him to the respectable and competitive Dallas Stars, you wonder if his tune has changed now that it's another sorry season in Columbus.

Now that Columbus has already bitten the Kirill Marchenko bullet, you wonder if you'll see more trades now that the team has taken a nosedive. Dmitri Voronkov could sure use a change of scenery for one.

The Red Wings have been a mess since Dylan Larkin's trade request and suspension. Now that they're 7-10-3 and riding a five-game losing streak, you'd think there would be increased urgency to trade him.

Keeping him on the roster while he just sits there might feel good for petty reasons, and yeah, it's unfortunate how this all played out. But the Red Wings are only hurting themselves until they bite the bullet, trade him, and start looking towards the future.

Looking beyond the Larkin saga, John Gibson, Justin Faulk, and Andrew Copp are all pending unrestricted free agents. Even though none of those players alone are going to yield gigantic returns, the Red Wings could stock up on assets that would better serve them in the future if they trade these players as rentals to contenders.

The bad news? LA's strategy of signing the oldest players possible isn't exactly working out. The good news? The oldest roster in the league has too many veterans to count that they could trade for some younger vibes.

Could they ship Erik Haula off to his 200th team? Could Scott Laughton be of service to a playoff team needing some extra edge and leadership? Any takers on Corey Perry?

The list goes on. It'll be fascinating to see if the Kings are willing to admit they made a mistake and act accordingly, or if they double down and don't make changes to the roster.

We anticipated that the Flyers would take a step back this season following their flukey two-round playoff run, but woof. They're 5-10-6, have the worst goal differential in the East at -22, and now questions surrounding Matvei Michkov's future are arising.

The Flyers aren't just taking a step back from last season's happy-go-lucky run; it looks like they're going to miss the playoffs entirely. They've long had a few fundamental pieces they've needed to address to consistently compete, most notably that gaping hole at first-line center.

Philly has a slew of underperforming veterans right now, so selling low might not be the best option. But if Travis Konecny, Cam York, Sean Couturier, or Owen Tippett start turning it on, any one of those players could yield a return that could help the team in the long run.

When's the last time the Canucks haven't been trading veterans in a rebuild? It feels like they've been in a rebuild forever, and yet there are miles to go before they rest.

They've got just three wins this season at 3-16-1 and a -34 goal differential. Honestly, almost every player on this roster should be considered on the table as the Canucks try to round the corner on this rebuild and get to the positive part. Elias Pettersson is putting together a decent season -- is it time to finally part ways? Jake DeBrusk is always an enticing playoff scoring depth option. Even Paul Cotter had a hot start that the Canucks could capitalize on on the trade market.

articles.title: New Rumor Offers NY Yankees Fantastic Upgrade Option at 3B, But It Comes With a BIG Risk
articles.summary: With the New York Yankees in search of an upgrade at third base, a two-time All-Star in his prime could […]
articles.body:
With the New York Yankees in search of an upgrade at third base, a two-time All-Star in his prime could be had at a reasonable price. But a potential trade comes with a big risk.

Despite winning 93 games while being in the same division as the American League Champion Tampa Bay Rays , the Yankees had some obvious weaknesses this season. Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. frustrated fans during a down year. Third baseman Ryan McMahon continued to disappoint at the plate after being acquired before the 2025 trade deadline. And homegrown product Austin Wells was an automatic out all season.

Replacing Wells is unlikely this offseason, and either Anthony Volpe or Luis Garcia Jr. is likely to take over at 2B in 2027. However, third base is a position the Yankees are working hard to upgrade after general manager Brian Cashman said it is "without a doubt" a top priority at this week's GM meeting in Las Vegas.

Unfortunately, the free agent market isn't overflowing with great options. Philadelphia Phillies veteran Alec Bohm is reportedly on the club's wish list, but according to FanSided's Robert Murray, " one name that I hear is popular is Phillies free agent Alec Bohm ." So the Yankees might have to engage in an unfavorable bidding war for the one-time All-Star.

Could the New York Yankees make Isaac Paredes trade for a reasonable price?

That is why the trade market could be Cashman's route to improve the hot corner. Houston Astros star Isaac Paredes would be a great addition for New York this offseason, and according to ESPN's Alden Gonzalez, he could be acquired at a more reasonable rate than Yankees fans might have thought.

In a new report, the MLB insider noted that the Astros have a roster construction problem and moving either Christian Walker, Paredes, or Jeremy Pena could help fix the problem. However, with all three only having one season left on their deals, sources claim moving them is "really difficult" because teams are having trouble justifying a trade with "uncertainty of how many games — if any — will be played in 2027."

It is good news for the Yankees if they are willing to take the risk. Paredes is a far better hitter than McMahon — he posted a .262 AVG, .806 OPS, 25 home runs, and 96 RBIs last season — and is a versatile infielder who can play first, second, and third base. If other teams are wary of a trade before a lockout, it could drive down the price and limit the competitors.

However, the possibility of lost games or an entire lost season is a good reason to be hesitant about giving up assets for a player they won't get a full season out of. Nevertheless, Paredes would be a very good addition to the lineup for next season. If the Astros want to add starting pitching this offseason, the Yankees can offer some solid and affordable options, along with solid prospects in a deal.

articles.title: Is Jalen Suggs playing tonight? Magic vs. Bucks injury report
articles.summary: The Orlando Magic could receive a significant boost ahead of Friday night’s NBA Cup matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks, as guard Jalen Suggs has been upgrad...
articles.body:
The Orlando Magic could receive a significant boost ahead of Friday night's NBA Cup matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks, as guard Jalen Suggs has been upgraded to questionable with a right knee contusion and bone bruise.

Orlando's latest injury report Friday morning listed the 25-year-old as questionable, signaling a potential return after missing the team's previous eight games.

The Magic (4-7) will host the struggling Bucks (1-11) at the Kia Center, with tipoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Suggs last appeared in Orlando's 111-102 victory over the New York Knicks on Oct. 25. He finished with four points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals across 34 minutes, shooting 2-for-8 from the field and 0-for-3 from beyond the arc.

Through three appearances this season, Suggs is averaging eight points, 5.7 assists, five rebounds and two steals while shooting 35.7% from the field and 11.1% from 3-point range in 33.3 minutes per game.

His potential return would provide additional backcourt depth for first-year head coach Sean Sweeney, whose team has struggled with injuries throughout the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign.

Orlando enters Friday riding a two-game winning streak following Wednesday's 123-108 victory over the Utah Jazz , which concluded its four-game road trip.

Jalen Suggs' potential return could provide crucial boost for injury-riddled Magic

Despite the encouraging update on Suggs, Orlando continues to deal with several notable injuries.

Star forward Paolo Banchero remains out with a right high ankle sprain, which has sidelined him since the team's Oct. 23 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Forward Tristan da Silva is questionable with a left calf strain, while Jamal Cain is also questionable because of a left shoulder contusion.

Meanwhile, Jonathan Isaac remains out due to left knee injury management, and Izaiyah Nelson continues recovering from a left ankle injury.

Second-year forward Noah Penda is also unavailable with a partially torn right hamstring.

With Orlando looking to extend its winning streak to three games, Suggs' availability could provide a timely boost against Milwaukee.

However, his questionable designation does not guarantee that he will play Friday night. The Magic will determine his final status closer to tipoff.

articles.title: San Joaquin County girls volleyball CIF State quarterfinal scores, recap
articles.summary: Four San Joaquin County girls volleyball teams entered Thursday's CIF State quarterfinals. Only two advanced. Here's every game recap and final score.
articles.body:
The first round couldn't have gone much better.

Only two of those four teams survived the quarterfinals Thursday, Nov. 12, keeping their state championship hopes alive.

Here's how each team fared, along with the scores and a full recap.

The lower the division number, the tougher the competition and the less separation there seems to be between seeds. St. Mary's is finding that out the hard way. Two days after being pushed to five sets by No. 16 Cardinal Newman , the top-seeded Rams needed another comeback to defeat No. 8 Harbor, the Santa Cruz Coast Athletic League champion and Central Coast Section Division III title winner. St. Mary's dropped the first and third sets before rallying for a 21-25, 25-18, 20-25, 25-16, 15-12 victory . According to MaxPreps, the Rams are ranked No. 73 in California, while Harbor sits just seven spots behind at No. 80. For a closer look at how St. Mary's survived, read The Record's full game story.

It's hard to believe a program could reach four straight CIF Sac-Joaquin Section championship games, win two of them and advance to the state tournament each year without winning a single state playoff match. Yet that was Ripon's reality over the previous four seasons. After the Indians fell in this year's CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division III championship , coach Gregory Soliz encouraged his players to turn that disappointment into something more. "Not a lot of teams can get to this point, and they did. At the same time, they're not happy about it I told them, let it hurt. Embrace the hurt. Then get ready for state." Apparently, his message got through. Ripon secured its second straight state tournament victory with a 25-15, 25-14, 25-15 sweep of Bullard, the County/Metro League runner-up. Setter Alayna Sprinkle recorded 31 assists and three kills, opposite and right-side hitter Jorie Eskes finished with 12 kills, and outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11. Outside hitter Ashlyn Malone made her presence felt with 10 kills, 11 digs and seven aces.

No. 3 Santa Cruz 3, No. 6 Ripon Christian 1

If there was ever a reminder of how slim the margins can be in the state tournament, Ripon Christian's nearly 100-mile trip to Santa Cruz provided one. The Knights took the opening set 25-23 against the Santa Cruz Coast League and Central Coast Section Division III runner-up, only to drop the next two by identical 25-23 scores before falling 25-18 in the fourth. Santa Cruz entered ranked No. 177 in California by MaxPreps compared with Ripon Christian at No. 337, but the Knights made the matchup much closer than those rankings suggested. Opposite hitter Alyssa Hofman had 17 kills, two blocks, 10 service points, three aces and 16 digs, while setter Rhian Heuvel added 22 assists and 18 digs. Libero Lauren Mouw collected a team-high 20 digs, 16 service points and four aces. Sophomore Bailey Brayton finished with nine kills and 17 digs, outside hitter Annika Jung had eight kills, Sabala recorded four kills and four blocks, Krista Koolhaas added five kills and Brooklynn Postma contributed 17 assists.

The seeds suggested an upset. The teams' resume suggested otherwise. Bear River had already proven itself with a perfect 14-0 Pioneer Valley League record, an appearance in the CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division V championship and 35 total wins. Against second-seeded Escalon, the No. 10 Bruins backed up that resume with a 25-20, 25-19, 25-21 sweep. MaxPreps currently ranks Bear River No. 152 in California and Escalon No. 172, another reminder that the gap between the teams wasn't necessarily reflected in their seeds. Senior setter Aniston Hunt finished with 25 assists, six digs, two kills, a block and an ace. Sophomore opposite and setter Avery Bartelink had 10 kills, 15 digs and an ace, while junior outside hitter Emma Strong added 13 kills and six digs.

articles.title: ‘Lean Strongly Toward (Kyrie) Irving Staying Put’ – NBA Insider Deals a Blow To Heat, Rockets in Trade Sweepstakes for Mavericks Star
articles.summary: Amid speculation surrounding Kyrie Irving’s future, The Athletic’s Sam Amick believes that the 34-year-old will likely remain with the Dallas Mavericks throu...
articles.body:
Amid speculation surrounding Kyrie Irving's future, The Athletic's Sam Amick believes that the 34-year-old will likely remain with the Dallas Mavericks through the Feb. 11 trade deadline.

The NBA insider made that call Friday, one day after the Mavericks' blowout loss in Minnesota, even while reporting that rival teams continue to rank Irving first among the players who could reshape the playoff race.

Why Insider Sees Kyrie Irving Staying With the Dallas Mavericks

Amick built his case around what is working in Dallas rather than around any one suitor. Miami has been reported as a team monitoring Irving, while Houston has also been floated as a possible fit if Dallas ever makes him available.

Amick led his latest trade-watch column with Irving, roughly three months before the deadline, and he did not skip past the lopsided result from the night before.

"Kyrie Irving may not be traded before the deadline, what with the Mavericks (7-5) looking better than expected and their 34-year-old point guard fitting in so well alongside their young franchise centerpiece, 19-year-old Cooper Flagg."

Amick pointed to the larger sample. By his count, the Mavericks are 7-3 this season when Irving plays and have lost both games he missed. But Amick wrote that the start in Dallas has not changed how rival teams see Irving.

"Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact."

Irving's contract helps explain why the interest persists. He holds a $42.4 million player option for next season and can become a free agent this summer if he declines it. "The lack of a long-term deal between the Mavs and Irving, all by itself, justifies the outside interest," Amick wrote.

So does his form. Irving missed all of last season after tearing his left ACL in early March 2025, and Amick noted that "the fact that Irving still looks like Irving, after all he has been through, has only added to the intrigue."

Asked about the rumors Monday, Irving told reporters, "I let the team know out of my own mouth that these trade rumors, anything that's going on with me, do not let this infiltrate our locker room. Don't let this get in the way of what we have building here."

Amick also explained why Dallas wants to get the most out of Irving. The Mavericks do not have outright control of their own first-round pick until 2031, which he wrote leaves them "otherwise limited in ways to surround Flagg with talent."

But Amick tied his forecast to how Dallas plays. "Things can always change, of course. But the odds of Irving being traded are likely notably less – if not nonexistent – if these Mavericks manage to play winning basketball," he wrote.

Even a quiet deadline would not settle Irving's future in Dallas, because his player option leaves the next decision with him this summer. The Mavericks, meanwhile, sit 10th in the Western Conference at 7-5 after Thursday's loss.

articles.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson ruled out vs. Detroit Lions

articles.body:
As Detroit (6-2) finalizes its week of practice ahead of its Sunday clash against New England (5-4) from Munich, Germany, the Patriots have ruled out running back TreVeyon Henderson for Sunday's game due to a recent illness.

In addition to Henderson, the Patriots also ruled out offensive lineman Ben Brown and former Lions cornerback Carlton Davis III.

The former Ohio State Buckeye released a statement on Friday, Nov. 6, that detailed his complications with a sudden and unexpected medical emergency that required hospitalization . As the symptoms have affected his strength, coordination, and other physical functions, it is no surprise that Henderson would be ruled out for the international game.

Detroit also released its Friday game status report , listing receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and running back Sione Vaki as questionable.

The Lions and Patriots kick off on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET, from Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, and the game will be broadcast on FOX.

articles.title: Red Wings Must End the John Gibson Experiment in Net
articles.summary: Another lead gone in Florida, and John Gibson's hold on the Red Wings net looks shakier than ever. #RedWings
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings once led 4-1 against the Florida Panthers on Thursday night. It ended in a 5-4 loss for Detroit. With the loss, the Red Wings have now lost five straight games, but the streak may not be the biggest story. John Gibson is.

Gibson stopped 24 of the 29 shots he faced in Florida, and he gave up five goals. That was not a one-night problem. Detroit has played 20 games this season and Gibson has appeared in 13 of them, and he carries a 4-7-1 record with a 3.58 goals-against average and a .862 save percentage , along with zero shutouts. With another bad outing on the pile, it might be time for the Red Wings to finally do something about it.

Detroit Red Wings need to end the John Gibson experiment now

The Red Wings are in last place in the Atlantic Division with a 7-10-3 record and 17 points . Detroit has a better chance to win in net right now with Daniil Tarasov, Michal Postava, or Trey Augustine.

There is no doubt that Gibson has been a major reason why the Red Wings have been losing. Look, the forward group is not deep by any means. With that being said, Gibson has not played well at all for Detroit this season. Who cares if he has a $6.4 million contract for the remainder of the season. The Red Wings need to seriously consider just scratching him until they can find a trade partner for him, or better yet place him on waivers.

Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava would be more beneficial to the team anyways

Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava from the Grand Rapids Griffins would be more beneficial to the growth of this hockey team than head coach Todd McLellan continuing to put Gibson between the pipes night in and night out. The Red Wings face the Tampa Bay Lightning on the road on Saturday. If they play Gibson again, this franchise is unserious about its goalie situation and cares more about tanking for a draft pick.

articles.title: Here's How Much Steelers vs. Bengals Means for Playoff Positioning, Division Race
articles.summary: This is the biggest game of the year for both teams.
articles.body:
When the Steelers travel to play the Bengals on Sunday night, it marks the biggest game of the season so far for Pittsburgh.

Both the Steelers and Bengals are 6-2 entering the game, with Pittsburgh ahead in the standings thanks to a win over Cincinnati earlier this season. As a result, the winner of this game will take the spot atop the AFC North standings, which would mean owning one of the top four seeds in AFC playoff positioning.

Even with that in play, the game means much more than just a temporary first-place spot. Whoever wins this game will increase their odds to make the playoffs and win the AFC North by a significant margin while also delivering a blow to the loser's chances at winning the division and earning a postseason spot.

Here's a breakdown of how much this game means for the Steelers.

The Steelers' game this weekend against the Bengals on Sunday night is Pittsburgh's biggest game of the season, as proven by the team's playoff odds. A win would give the Steelers an inside track towards winning the division, while a loss would drop them to a wild-card spot.

Playoff probability with win: 89% (+10%)

Playoff probability with loss: 72% (-7%)

A win by the Steelers would improve their chances of making the playoffs by 10 percent, according to NFL.com , while a loss would drop their chances by 7 percent. That largely accounts for the AFC North title, as Pittsburgh would take a commanding lead in the division with a victory.

The Bengals have a 92 percent chance of making the playoffs entering the week, which is mainly because of Cincinnati's easy schedule down the stretch. However, a loss would drop the Bengals' odds below the Steelers' odds and force Cincinnati to think about earning a Wild Card slot.

Therefore, it's fair to say that the AFC North is on the line this weekend, as the winner would take full control of the division moving forward. A Steelers win would not only give Pittsburgh a one-game lead, but also secure the Steelers the tiebreaker over the Bengals, while a loss would give the Bengals a one-game lead with an easier schedule remaining.

While the Browns and Ravens are still alive in the division race, it seems as though the AFC North winner will be either the Steelers or the Bengals. So, it is crucial for Pittsburgh to treat this game like a playoff game and come away 2-0 against the Bengals this season.

articles.title: ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’: Maxx Crosby says Joe Burrow is ‘the closest person we’ve seen’ to Tom Brady
articles.summary: Over the past several years, Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow has emerged as one of the top quarterbacks in the league. But longtime veter...
articles.body:
Over the past several years, Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow has emerged as one of the top quarterbacks in the league. But longtime veteran star pass rusher Maxx Crosby wants everyone to know just how good he truly is.

During a recent interview, Crosby said that if you "know ball," you truly understand just how good Burrow is, as he went as far as to compare him to Tom Brady.

Burrow and the Bengals are rolling right now. Cincinnati beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid last week to improve to 6-2, extending its winning streak to four games.

Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in the win, while also running in a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a score, and Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns.

Burrow's 21 passing touchdowns lead the NFL. He also leads the league in completion percentage and is second in the league in passing yards, behind only Jordan Love. And he has been getting plenty of love lately. Earlier this week, ESPN's Louis Riddick said on The Dan Patrick Show that Burrow is "that guy" and that there's no other quarterback he would take over him.

Crosby discussed Burrow and Chase on the latest episode of his podcast, The Rush with Maxx Crosby . He made it clear he has been a Burrow believer for a long time.

"He's one of the best quarterbacks in the league. I've been saying that since, you know, since day one," Crosby said.

"So, yeah, if you know ball, you realize how good Joe Burrow is. He's the most comparable, in my opinion. This is, and obviously there's still levels and all that, but he's the most comparable to Tom Brady in the way he plays in my eyes. I think he's the closest person we've seen in that regard. Now, you got to go get seven of them, you know, to really be in that world. I'm sure of it, you know, but yeah, just the way he plays, the way he operates, and his pocket presence, I think, is the best thing about his game," Crosby said.

Crosby did have one piece of advice for Burrow, who has dealt with several injuries during his career.

"Now, he takes some unnecessary blows. Even if you put a flag, even if he's playing flag football, for some reason, Joe Burrow loves to take the worst spills of all time. If somebody can just get in there with [him] maybe and figure out how to land a little, like, more gracefully, I think would maybe do wonders for him," Crosby continued.

That's high praise coming from one of the best pass rushers in the league.
